content.content:
**Article date:** October 22, 2026 (published on the Tella blog, so the comparison is written by one of the vendors.)

**Tella**
- **Auto-zoom:** Generated from the Effect panel with Adaptive, Subtle, Moderate, or Intense settings. Each zoom can be moved, retargeted, split, or deleted.
- **Platforms:** Mac, Windows, web recorder, and Chrome extension.
- **Sharing:** Hosted page with viewer analytics, comments, password protection, branding, and embeds.
- **Pricing:** No free plan, but a 7-day trial. From $13/user/mo on annual Pro.
- **Stated weaknesses:** Built for demos, tutorials, courses, and async video, not for game recording or frame-by-frame VFX editing.

**Screen Studio**
- **Auto-zoom:** Follows clicks, with edits made in its timeline.
- **Platforms:** macOS only.
- **Sharing:** Links for videos up to 30 minutes each, with comments and view counts. Mainly built for exporting files up to 4K/60.
- **Pricing:** From $9/mo. No free plan.
- **Stated weaknesses:** Mac-only, 30-minute link cap, analytics limited to view counts, no team plan.

**Cap**
- **Auto-zoom:** Generated, with editable zoom segments.
- **Platforms:** Mac and Windows.
- **Sharing:** Hosted share links. Free cloud links are limited to 5 minutes; paid plans remove the limit.
- **Pricing:** Free tier. Paid from $29/yr.
- **Stated weaknesses:** Younger product with a smaller editing feature set and no blur effect.

**FocuSee**
- **Auto-zoom:** Generates zooms and cursor effects automatically.
- **Platforms:** Mac and Windows.
- **Sharing:** Paid plans only.
- **Pricing:** From $49.99/yr, or a $199.99 lifetime licence. No free plan.
- **Stated weaknesses:** Hosting is a paid add-on rather than a core feature, and there's no team workspace.

**Supercut**
- **Auto-zoom:** Generated automatically.
- **Platforms:** Mac and Windows.
- **Sharing:** Hosted page for each video.
- **Pricing:** From €13/seat/mo. No free plan.
- **Stated weaknesses:** No blur or highlight, so private on-screen content needs another tool.

**Camtasia**
- **Auto-zoom:** Generated inside a detailed timeline editor with more manual control.
- **Platforms:** Mac and Windows.
- **Sharing:** No hosting. Videos are exported and uploaded to another host.
- **Pricing:** From $179.88/yr. No free plan.
- **Stated weaknesses:** Every share requires an export and upload step.

**Loom (reference only):** No automatic zooms, but strong hosting. Blur is paid-only. Free plan allows 5-minute recordings.

This part of the changelog starts partway through an entry near the top, so anything newer than the first visible heading (June 8, 2026) isn't included. Entries are listed newest first, grouped by topic.

**API & MCP**
- **Dec 18, 2025 (API and MCP):** The public API and MCP server launched, giving access to videos, transcripts, and playlists, plus an SDK and a Zapier integration. This is the earliest API/MCP launch in this part.
- **May 8, 2026 (Clip API):** Clips became first-class API resources, with CRUD, cuts, transcripts, zooms, blurs, highlights, and layouts, all with matching MCP tools.
- **May 13, 2026:** Video upload through the API (`POST /v1/sources`), with video media in layouts and new MCP tools.
- **May 22, 2026:** Multi-range clip cuts and cut-by-transcript-word endpoints.

**Auto zoom**
- **Sep 24, 2024 (Auto Zoom):** Analyzes clicks and cursor movement to add zooms automatically, for videos recorded with the Mac app.
- **Sep 5, 2025:** Zoom intensity preferences (Subtle, Moderate, Energetic).
- **Sep 24, 2025 (Auto Zooms V2):** New algorithm, style presets, and animation settings.
- **Feb 14, 2023 (Zooms):** Manual zoom-in and zoom-out effects, which predate auto zoom.

**Transcript editing**
- **May 2, 2024 (Text-Based Editing):** Edit video by editing its text, cutting words, phrases, or sentences.
- **Dec 12, 2025:** Transcript dictionary and find-and-replace.
- **Aug 22, 2025:** Create clips from transcript selections via "Copy to new video."
- **Apr 10, 2026:** Cutting words from the transcript also trims surrounding silence.
- **Apr 16, 2026:** A persistent transcript sidebar in the new editor.

**Remove mistakes, fillers, and silences**
- **Apr 30, 2024 (AI Editing Tools):** Auto-trim recording, remove filler words, remove silences, and auto-cut start and end.
- **Jul 22, 2025 (Auto Cut):** Finds mistakes, repeated lines, and interruptions and removes them in one click.
- **May 22, 2026:** Silence detection combines waveform amplitude with voice activity detection.

**Clips and shorts**
- **Mar 22, 2024:** AI-generated clip titles.
- **Aug 22, 2025:** Creating new videos from transcript selections.
- **May 15, 2026:** Rendered clips are saved to the media library for reuse as B-roll or intros.
- **Jun 5, 2026:** Restore removed clips.
- **Social safe zones (May 22, 2026):** Overlays for Reels, TikTok, Shorts, and LinkedIn on portrait videos.

**Translation and dubbing**
- **Feb 28, 2024 (More languages):** 13 new subtitle languages, bringing the total to 20. No dubbing appears in this part.

**AI voice**
- **Aug 26, 2025 (Studio Voice):** AI-powered audio enhancement that removes background noise and boosts volume.
- **Jun 8, 2026:** Studio Voice can be turned off per clip.

**Layouts**
- **Nov 28, 2023 and Dec 20, 2023 (Multi-Layouts):** Switch between multiple layouts within a video.
- **Jan 15, 2024 (Transitions):** Hard cut and smooth transitions between layouts.
- **Jul 10, 2025 (Auto Layouts):** Pick a template and generate layouts automatically.
- **Oct 24, 2025 (Layouts V2):** Adding a layout became a single click-and-drag action.
- **Nov 20, 2025 (Custom Layouts):** Create, save, and reuse your own layouts.
- **Apr 17, 2026:** Side-by-side 50/50 layout and TV Presenter full-frame variants.
- **May 18, 2026 (Auto layouts v2):** Portrait and square support, plus AI-generated image B-roll.

Prequel is a macOS screen recorder that automatically edits your recordings. The official site describes it as a screen recorder for macOS that does the editing for you.

**Key features:**
- **Automatic zooms:** Zooms follow your cursor, clicks, and typing. It zooms into the part of the screen that matters: the cursor, a region you draw, or whatever you are typing into.
- **Camera and background:** The webcam is framed, with a background and rounded corners. Prequel offers ten layouts, switchable mid-take.
- **Separate tracks:** Prequel records screen, camera, microphone and system audio as separate tracks in one take.
- **Transcription:** Captions are transcribed on your Mac when you stop, in your Mac's language, and you fix a word by typing over it.
- **Export:** Export is one MP4 at up to 4K, rendered on your Mac's own media engine. One blog claims up to 4K and 120 fps, though other sources say 60fps for Screen Studio.
- **Privacy:** Recording, editing and export all happen locally, on your Mac's own media engine.

**Requirements and limits:** It needs an Apple Silicon Mac on macOS 14 or later, and there is no Intel or Windows support.

**Pricing (sources disagree):** Prequel's own blog says Prequel is $39, once. with a seven-day trial that exports finished files before you pay. A different Prequel blog post instead lists $29 once or $9 a month. Check prequel.sh for current pricing.

Sources: prequel.sh (official site), prequel.sh blog posts, Product Hunt, and third-party directories. The directories mostly repeat the official marketing, so the feature claims are largely self-reported.

To see 2025 releases and earlier 2026 versions, use "Load more" on the changelog page or check the full changelog.

## Prequel: Claimed Features

**Version and date:** v0.8.1, with a changelog entry described as "A cut-out layout for the camera." The footer reads © 2026.

**Pricing:** The page doesn't list prices. It links to a Pricing page and says "Free for 7 days. No watermark on anything you export." It also says "No credit card required."

**Platform requirements:**
- Apple Silicon Mac (the page says "Apple Silicon · macOS 14+")
- Screen Recording permission
- Accessibility permission, needed only for typing-driven zooms. Without it, that input is absent.

### Recording
- **Capture sources:** a display, a window, or a dragged area.
- **Separate tracks:** camera, microphone, and system audio, each on its own track with separate gains.
- **Native capture:** uses the system's own capture and the Mac's video hardware for encoding.

### Zoom and Pan
- **Automatic zooms:** triggered by clicks and typing, then softened on the rest of the window.
- **Zoom targets:** cursor, a drawn region, or the field being typed into.
- **Adjustable controls:** level, speed, tilt, yaw, and blur falloff, set per zoom.
- **Editable zooms:** each one is a normal timeline slice that can be moved, retimed, or deleted.

### Layouts
- **Fourteen layouts**, with names shown in the UI: Full, Padded, Beside, Stacked, Split, and Camera.
- **Per-clip switching:** one layout for the whole video, or a different one for each clip.

### Camera
- **Shapes:** circle, squircle, rounded, wide, and portrait.
- **Adjustable placement:** any corner, any size, and mirroring.
- **Non-destructive:** the camera is never burned into the recording, so these settings can change after recording.

### Subtitles
- **Automatic transcription:** runs on the Mac when the editor opens.
- **Text editing:** fix captions by typing in the transcript, or delete a sentence to remove it from the video.
- **Subtitle styles:** named in the UI as Blur in, Subtitle, Highlight, and Band, plus an Edit option.

### Teleprompter
- **Script display:** shown beneath the camera notch.
- **Voice tracking:** highlights each word as it's spoken.
- **Off-script handling:** pauses when you go off script and catches up within a couple of words when you skip ahead or fall behind.

### Editor
- **Automatic opening:** opens on the take as soon as you stop recording.
- **Timeline actions:** Add Zoom, Add Text, and Add Clip.
- **Speed:** 0.25×, 0.5×, 1×, 2×, and 4×.
- **Frame settings:** Landscape 16:9 at 1920×1080, padding, corner radius, border width and color (#2A2D33), border opacity, shadow opacity, shadow blur, and shadow offset.
- **Trimming:** cut clips slice by slice, with a waveform under each clip.
- **Backgrounds:** your own wallpaper by default, seven bundled presets, gradients, and solids.
- **Pointer:** fifteen pointer styles, resized to stay visible during zooms, smoothed while moving, and hidden after a few seconds of stillness.
- **Preview fidelity:** the preview and export draw the same plan.

### Export and Quality
- **Format:** one MP4 in H.264 or HEVC.
- **Resolution and frame rate:** up to 4K and up to 120 fps, constant frame rate.
- **Recording quality:** 1080p at 60 fps without dropped frames.
- **Encoding and compositing:** hardware encoding through VideoToolbox and drawing in Metal.
- **Frame presets:** 16:9, 4K, vertical 9:16, square 1:1, portrait 4:5, and social presets for YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, Reels, X, and LinkedIn.
- **Format conversion:** framing is stored as proportions, so a layout survives a switch from landscape to vertical.
- **Sharing:** you can create a link that "plays anywhere" for a finished export. The page says this step involves an upload.

### Privacy
- Recording, editing, and export happen locally. The page says there is no upload step and no cloud render, except when you request a shareable link.

**Record for agent: summary**

- **What it does:** A recording mode in Loom that turns short screen recordings into prompts for AI agents. It captures your narrated transcript, screenshots of elements you click, and links you visit during the recording. You can send the prompt directly to an agent from Loom or open it as a Jira work item assigned to an agent. The new Loom for Mac also adds a Selection tool and Magic pen to point out UI elements and annotate the screen.
- **Date:** October 22, 2026
- **Plan availability:** Loom Business + AI and Enterprise plans
- **Status:** Open beta
- **Platforms:** New Loom for Mac or the Loom Chrome extension
- **MCP integration:** Record for agent is separate from MCP, but Loom tools in Atlassian MCP let agents such as Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, and Rovo access Loom recordings. Agents can pull transcripts, metadata, and action items, add timestamped comments, and share or organize recordings within existing Loom permissions. Users on Atlassian MCP v2 get these tools automatically once their Loom workspace is linked to their Atlassian site. Users on v1 need to upgrade.

content.content:
## Features

- **Screen recording:** Records the screen, with auto-zoom that follows the cursor and zooms on clicks and keystrokes during capture.
- **Cursor tracking:** Auto-zoom follows the cursor as you record.
- **Editing:** Transcript-based cutting, a built-in editor, pause, and speeding up or removing sections.
- **Captions:** Adds captions. Transcription runs on-device with WhisperKit (Apple Silicon) or in the cloud if enabled.
- **Visual styling:** Background colors, gradients, or wallpapers; padding; rounded corners; shadows; and a movable, resizable camera overlay.
- **B-roll:** Mentioned in the creator use case.
- **Export:** Up to 1080p60 and H.264, using the hardware encoder.
- **AI agent editing:** Works with Claude Code, Codex, Grok, and Kimi. The page cites 83 agent tools, each with a dry run before changes are committed. It also shows a CLI command, `screenkite agent export --json`. The page does not mention MCP, so MCP support is not confirmed.

## Pricing

- **Free:** Recording and editing are free. Exports include a watermark.
- **Pro:** $79.99 one-time payment, covering 3 Macs, with no subscription or renewal. It rises to $99.99 after Oct 31, 2026.
- **AI fees:** None from ScreenKite. AI usage is billed to the user's own agent plan.

## Platform

- **macOS:** Requires macOS 15 or later, on Apple Silicon or Intel.
- **Transcription:** WhisperKit requires Apple Silicon. Intel Macs use ElevenLabs cloud transcription.
- **Windows:** A Windows beta is mentioned, with no details given.

## Version and date info

- **ScreenKite 1.18:** Version used in the speed benchmark.
- **Benchmark date:** September 2026, comparing against Screen Studio 2.x.
- **Founder pricing deadline:** October 31, 2026.

The "3x faster" export claim comes from the vendor's own benchmark and is not independently verified.

**Screen Studio 4.0: reported problems (Sept 27 to Oct 12, 2026)**

*Source note: The article is published by ScreenKite, a competing product, so its claims are unverified. Its 4.0 bug reports come from the official Screen Studio Telegram group, X posts, and team replies. Its Reddit citations concern pricing, not 4.0 bugs.*

**Export failures**
- **Sept 30 (Telegram):** A user said three hours of work was destroyed after a conversion error.
- **Oct 2 (Telegram):** An error reported that a frame "could not be decoded after 3 attempts." Kaya said developers were "currently working on a fix."
- **Oct 3 and Oct 11 (Telegram):** Exports stalled at 95% and at 0%.
- **Oct 7–8 (Telegram):** A user reported exports still failing after updating.
- **X, @HariBonda:** Batch exports failing overnight since v4, and the user asked how to return to v3.
- **X, @attacomsian:** Memory reportedly spiked to 8.43 GB while exporting a one-minute 4K video.

**Black editor on Intel Macs**
- **Oct 2 (Telegram):** The editor was black, including for old projects.
- **Oct 6 (Telegram):** A 2019 Intel MacBook Pro showed a blank screen for old and new projects. Kaya called it "a known issue."
- **Oct 8 (Telegram):** An Intel MacBook Pro with an AMD Radeon Pro 5500M showed a black preview and failed exports.
- **X, @theDanielJLewis:** Screen and camera not recording properly in v4, and the user suspected an Intel problem.
- **Screen Studio team member, X:** Pointed @uiux_hamad to the beta, citing an issue with Intel Macs that have AMD GPUs. Hamad said he would rather not use a beta.

**Features removed "temporarily"**
- **Oct 1–9:** Users asked where "Improve microphone audio," audio enhancement, mono-to-stereo, and mic boost went.
- **Oct 4–5 (Kaya):** Audio enhancement features were "temporarily in Screen Studio Beta."
- **Oct 7 (Oktawia):** VoiceOver was still being fixed and was being brought back, with no completion date.
- **X, @direwolfram:** Asked whether the microphone feature was removed in the latest version.

**New regressions**
- **Oct 3 (Telegram):** Mouse size set to zero in every clip, cut sections still playing, and footage appearing in the wrong projects.
- **Oct 7, v4.0.4 (Telegram):** Cursor jumps added automatically with no way to disable them.
- **Oct 12, v4.0.4 (Telegram):** Audio playing about 1.5 seconds earlier than the waveform showed.

**Pricing and support**
- **Oct 8:** A lifetime license holder was offered an upgrade for USD 89 per year.
- **Oct 8 (Telegram):** A user said their support messages were deleted. Another said a submitted ticket had received no response. Oktawia apologized the next day.

**Crashes (X)**
- **Sept 24, Oct 2, Oct 3:** Several users reported crashes during recording or export, mostly on MacBook Air.

**Screen Studio statement (X, Oct 12)**
- The founder announced a new export engine, saying a 38-second project exports in 4.8 seconds.

**What was rolled back**
- Audio enhancement features, including "Improve microphone audio," mono-to-stereo, and mic boost, were moved to Screen Studio Beta. On Oct 9, the team said "We've temporarily rolled back these features." No return date was given.
- VoiceOver was also pulled back for fixes, with no return date.

**Release timeline:** The article lists four 4.0.x releases between Oct 3 and Oct 8. Users said exports still failed after several of them.

Camtasia's cursor smoothing, path editing, and elevation features are documented in TechSmith's tutorials and product pages.

**Cursor smoothing:** It only works on recordings captured with Camtasia. You add it from the Cursor Effects tab by dragging it onto a clip, then adjust its settings in the Properties panel. Dragging the left or right edge of the effect changes its length. The Duration setting controls how long the cursor takes to travel between points. Detect Cursor Pauses shows stationary moments of one second or longer in the cursor path.

**Cursor path editing:** In Camtasia Recording (TREC) files, you can fix the cursor position when it doesn't match the narration, or smooth out movements after recording. For footage not recorded in Camtasia, the Cursor Path Creator effect lets you design a cursor path. You can also build a custom path and add clicks on any image, video, or TREC file.

**Elevation:** This is set in the Properties panel under the Cursor Properties tab, using the Elevation dropdown and choosing "Always on Top." Cursor elevation lifts the pointer above callouts, annotations, and effects so it doesn't get lost in the visuals.

content.content:
ScreenKite's approach is that an AI agent edits the recording itself, on the user's machine, instead of turning the recording into a prompt for another tool. The page does not describe a CLI or MCP server, so I can't confirm either.

**How it works**
- You record in ScreenKite, which captures the full screen and applies auto-zoom based on cursor and click activity.
- You tell an agent what edit you want. The page's example is "Cut the pauses, zoom on the clicks, export for YouTube."
- Supported agents are Claude Code, ChatGPT Codex, Antigravity, Grok Build, and Kimi.
- The agent uses the same editing tools as the app's interface, so agent edits and manual edits share one tool surface.

**Safety and review**
- The page says meaning-changing edits, such as timeline or transcript cuts, first return a plan when called with `confirm:false`. They apply only when called with `confirm:true`. This is the closest the page comes to a dry run.
- In the Core Agent chat panel, the user approves changes by risk tier.
- Because agent edits go through the same tools as clicks, the page says they can be undone the same way.

**Billing**
- Agent usage is billed to the agent subscription the user already has.
- The ScreenKite AI fee is $0.

**Dates and counts**
- Loom announced Record for Agent in open beta on October 7, 2026.
- The ScreenKite article was published October 7, 2026, last updated October 19, 2026, and facts were checked October 7, 2026.
- ScreenKite has 83 editing tools.
- The page lists 5 supported agents.
- The one-time Pro price is $79.99, covering 3 devices, with no renewal. The founder price lasts until October 31, 2026, then rises to $99.99.
- Recording has no five-minute cap, unlike Loom's Record for Agent.
- Requirements are macOS 15 or later, on Apple Silicon or Intel, with a native Windows Beta. An account is required.

**Caveats**
- This is vendor marketing. The page gives no independent verification of the tool counts or the agent behavior.
- The page doesn't say how the CLI or MCP would connect agents to the app, or whether a dry run is a separate mode. I've described only what it states.

**Cap 0.5.7 (Jul 20, 2026)**

- **Access:** Agents can use Cap through the expanded CLI, an installable skill, and a local MCP server, after a browser login.
- **Recording, exports, sharing:** Agents can "record, export, upload, and share."
- **Reading content:** Titles, transcripts, AI summaries, chapters, comments, reactions, views, permissions, and processing state.
- **Library and analytics:** Searching and organizing the library, and inspecting analytics.
- **Admin:** Managing collaboration, teams, storage, migrations, and developer workflows "without using the dashboard."
- **Safeguards:** Output is machine-readable JSON, changes need your confirmation, and secrets stay out of chat and MCP.

**Cap 0.5.1 (Jun 6, 2026)**

- **Recording:** Targets, screenshots, and detached recording sessions.
- **Projects and exports:** Listing recordings, inspecting and validating projects, and exporting.
- **Uploads and diagnostics:** Uploading, running doctor diagnostics, and printing machine-readable guide output.
- **Goal:** Let agents drive Cap "without relying on UI automation."
- **Not listed:** Transcripts, AI summaries, chapters, and sharing are not mentioned for this release.

**Timeline editing:** Neither release says agents can edit the timeline. Neither mentions zooms or cuts. The 0.5.1 project features are inspection and validation, and the 0.5.7 features are reading and organizing content, not changing edits. The editing features described in the page (for example, clip transitions and the zoom shortcut) are for people using the app.

**Rotato: Summary (verified August 20, 2026)**

**Features**
- Drag-and-drop images and videos onto 30+ hand-built phone, tablet, laptop, and desktop models
- Custom backgrounds, reflections, shadows, depth of field, virtual camera controls, and clay styles
- App Store screenshot sizes, batch workflows, and ready-made scene and video templates
- Figma workflows and an official Figma plugin
- iPhone mirroring and screen recording over USB
- Offline-first local rendering on Mac

**Device models:** 30+ phone, tablet, laptop, and desktop models

**Video and animation**
- Timeline-based camera and device animation
- Still and video rendering up to 8K
- Standard video in H.264 or HEVC (MOV or MP4)
- Transparent video in HEVC with alpha or Apple ProRes 4444
- Image sequences (PNG, JPG, WebP, or AVIF)
- Lottie JSON export for web animation
- Frame rates of 24, 30, 60, 120, or custom
- No direct WebM export; the free Rotato Converter handles conversion for Chromium-based browsers

**Pricing**
- Rotato for Mac: one-time paid plans, with an update period after which you can keep using the purchased version
- Rotato Web: priced separately
- Check the official pricing page for current terms

**Platforms**
- Rotato for Mac: native app for macOS 12 or newer, renders locally, works offline
- Rotato Web: browser-based option for Windows and other non-Mac desktops
- edit.rotato.app: experimental and not the default Windows recommendation

Across Capterra, G2, and vendor-competitor blogs, the main complaints about Camtasia match your query: a learning curve, the move to subscription pricing, and performance problems.

- **Learning curve:** G2's pros-and-cons summary lists a steep learning curve as a recurring complaint, reported in 42 reviews, while the same page notes that ease of use is what users like most ([G2](https://g2.com/products/camtasia/reviews?page=4)). Capterra reviewers are split. Some say the interface is not much harder than other editors ([Capterra AU](https://www.capterra.com.au/software/203013/camtasia)), and others call the learning curve small and manageable after a short adjustment period ([Capterra](https://capterra.com/p/203013/Camtasia/reviews/?page=7)).
- **Subscription:** Camtasia became subscription-only starting with the 2025 version, and new perpetual licenses are no longer sold ([Trainn](https://trainn.co/blog/what-is-camtasia/)). Reviewers on Capterra and G2 push back on the recurring cost, and one G2 reviewer complains that the app keeps requiring a server check even with a valid subscription ([G2](https://g2.com/products/camtasia/reviews?page=4)).
- **Performance:** Reviewers on Capterra report that the software is resource-heavy and needs strong hardware for longer edits ([Capterra NZ](https://www.capterra.co.nz/reviews/203013/camtasia)). Others report crashes on complex projects ([Capterra AU](https://www.capterra.com.au/reviews/203013/camtasia)). Audio sync problems also come up on G2 ([G2](https://g2.com/products/camtasia/reviews?page=4)).
- **Ratings:** G2 shows an aggregate of 4.6 out of 5 from 1,756 reviews ([G2](https://www.g2.com/products/Camtasia/reviews)). GetApp summarizes the pricing as relatively high, especially for individuals and small businesses ([GetApp](https://www.getapp.com/communication-software/a/camtasia/)).

**Caveats:** Several of the sources promoting alternatives (Trainn, Trupeer, Guidde) have a commercial stake in criticizing Camtasia, and their pricing figures conflict. Trupeer lists a $299.99 one-time license ([Trupeer](https://www.trupeer.ai/id/blog/camtasia-for-onboarding)), which contradicts the subscription-only policy reported elsewhere. Check the current prices on TechSmith's site before relying on any of them.

# Screen recording

Frame Job records your screen itself. You can record a whole display or a single window, with system audio, your microphone and rings around your clicks, and the recording goes straight into a project. You can also record a camera, on its own or beside the screen as a talking head in the corner, and a voice-over, which is the microphone alone with no picture, at the playhead of the project you're editing. Every recording is an ordinary movie or audio file on disk, and Frame Job imports it the way it imports any other media, so every edit, effect and export works on it.

## Opening the recorder

Choose **File ▸ New Recording…** (⌥⌘N), or click **New Recording…** on the welcome window. A small floating panel titled **New Recording** opens. You don't need a project open.

The panel floats above other windows and doesn't make Frame Job the active app when you click it. That lets you bring the app you want to record to the front and still press Record. It also doesn't hide when you switch to another app. If you open it while Frame Job is in the background, it comes to the front without taking the keyboard, so your typing stays in the app you were using.

In the panel, Return presses **Record** and Esc presses **Close**.

## The panel's controls

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Source** | What to record. Lists one row per connected display by name, then **Window…** (pick one window), then **Camera** (a camera on its own), then **Microphone Only** (a voice-over with no picture). | The display you used last, else the main display |
| **Include Frame Job windows** | Puts Frame Job's own windows, such as the editor and the preview, into a display recording. When it's off, they're left out of the picture. | Off |
| **Record the camera too** | With a display or **Window…** as the source, also records the chosen camera beside the screen (see [A camera beside the screen](#a-camera-beside-the-screen)). It's greyed out, keeping its value, with **Camera** or **Microphone Only**. | Off |
| **Camera** | With **Source** set to **Camera**, or with **Record the camera too** ticked, which camera to record: each connected camera by name, or **None connected**. An iPhone used as a Continuity Camera reads "<name> (Continuity Camera)". It's greyed out otherwise. | The camera you used last, else the Mac's preferred camera, then the first built-in camera, then the first one connected |
| **Format** | With **Source** set to **Camera**, or with **Record the camera too** ticked, the size and frame rate to record at. **Best** comes first and names the camera's best format, for example **Best (1760×1328 at 30 fps)**. Then come the camera's other formats, such as **1920×1080 at 30 fps**: sizes wider than tall first, then square, then taller than wide, each largest first and at its highest frame rate. It's greyed out otherwise. | The format you used last when the chosen camera has it, else Best |
| **Preview** | With **Source** set to **Camera**, or with **Record the camera too** ticked, a live picture of the chosen camera at the chosen format, under Format. It's shown as the movie will record it: not mirrored, the whole picture fitted inside. The row appears only then. | — |
| **Microphone** | **Off**, or one of the connected microphones. A live level meter sits beside it. | Off |
| **Enhance the microphone when it lands** | After the recording lands, runs [Enhance Voice](audio.md#enhance-voice) on the microphone's clips (see [Enhancing the microphone](#enhancing-the-microphone)). It works with any source, and it's greyed out, keeping its value, when **Microphone** is **Off** or a recording is under way. | Off |
| **System Audio** | Records what the system plays, as the movie's own stereo 48 kHz sound track. | On |
| **Show Clicks** | Draws a ring around each mouse click. The pointer itself is always recorded. | Off |
| **Rate** | **30 fps** or **60 fps**: the most frames per second the file may hold. It's also the frame rate of a new project made from the recording. | 60 fps |
| **Size** | **Nominal (points)** records the display at its point size. **Best (pixels)** records every pixel, which is twice the points on a Retina display. | Nominal (points) |
| **Record Into** | **New Project**, or any open project by name. | The front project, else New Project |

Under Size, a note shows what you'll get for the chosen display, for example `1728×1117 points · 3456×2234 pixels`. For a picked window it reads "the picked window's own size". For Microphone Only it reads "no picture — the microphone alone". For Camera it names the format the camera records at, for example `1760×1328 at 30 fps — the camera's best format` with Format set to Best, `1920×1080 at 30 fps — the chosen format` with a format chosen, or "no camera connected".

The footnote at the bottom left shows where recordings are saved (for example `saved in ~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`). While a recording runs, it shows the elapsed time instead.

The panel remembers your choices between uses, including the display, microphone, camera, camera format, switches, rate, size and the Include Frame Job windows, Record the camera too and Enhance the microphone when it lands boxes. The camera format is one choice for every camera: a camera that doesn't have the remembered format shows Best. It doesn't remember a picked window, the Camera or Microphone Only source (each lasts for the session only), or Record Into. A display, microphone or camera that is no longer connected falls back to the main display, to Off, or to the default camera. While the panel is up and not recording, the Camera and Microphone lists follow the devices you plug in or take away (a change made during a recording waits for it to end). A camera that's removed falls back to the default camera, and when it comes back it's chosen again with its format. Plugging in or removing a device doesn't change what the panel remembers.

### Record Into

**Record Into** follows whichever project is in front, until you choose a row yourself. After that it keeps your choice for as long as that project stays open. When you press Record, the row freezes, so switching to another window during the recording doesn't change where the recording goes.

## Choosing what to record

### A display

Choose a display by name in **Source**. Frame Job's own windows are left out of a display recording unless **Include Frame Job windows** is on. Even with the box on, the recorder panel itself is never in the picture. The panel leaves the screen as soon as the recording starts.

Frame Job's own sound is never recorded, with or without the box. That means you can play the timeline during a recording and it won't end up in the file.

### A window

Choose **Window…** in **Source** and macOS's window picker opens. Click the window you want. The Source row then reads **Window (picked)** and the recording is that window alone, at its own size. If you cancel the picker, Source goes back to the display you used last. If the picker can't open at all, Source also goes back to the display you used last, and the note reads "The window picker could not open: …" with the reason.

When **Include Frame Job windows** is off, the picker lists none of Frame Job's windows. When it's on, the picker lists them, but never the recorder panel. The box only changes the next time the picker opens. A window you've already picked stays picked.

If you press Record while the row reads **Window…** with nothing picked, the panel says "Choose a window with Window… first, or pick a display." and nothing records.

### A camera

Choose **Camera** in **Source**, then the camera in **Camera**:

- **System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size**, **Include Frame Job windows** and **Rate** grey out. Their values are kept for next time. A camera records at the format chosen in **Format**, at that format's highest frame rate. **Best** is the largest size wider than tall that runs at 30 fps or more. The note under Size names the format.
- **Microphone** and **Record Into** stay live. The microphone you choose, which can be the camera's own when macOS lists it, is recorded to its own file beside the movie. **Off** records the camera alone.
- With no camera connected, Record says "No camera is connected."
- Only the Camera permission (and the Microphone permission, when one is chosen) is checked. Screen Recording isn't needed.

The camera starts as soon as the panel shows **Camera**, and the **Preview** under Format shows its live picture. Because it's already running, it has settled at its frame rate by the time recording begins, and its light stays on while the panel shows **Camera**. Choosing a display or another source (unless **Record the camera too** is ticked there), or closing the panel, turns it off. The preview changes with the camera and format you choose. Instead of the picture it reads "No camera is connected." with no camera, "The preview shows once Frame Job may use the camera." until you've allowed the Camera permission (showing the panel never asks for it, pressing Record does), or the reason the camera couldn't start. Choosing **Camera** again or reopening the panel tries again. **The panel stays up** while a camera records, as it does for a voice-over: nothing on screen is filmed. Its controls lock, the meter stays live, the footnote shows ● or ❚❚ and the elapsed time, Record reads **Stop**, and a **Pause** / **Resume** button appears beside it. If you close the panel, the recording carries on.

The camera's movie lands like a screen recording's picture: on the front track if it fits, else on a new track in front, with the microphone on a new back track named **Microphone**. As a new project, the canvas is the movie's size at the format's frame rate. If the camera stops on its own (for example, it's unplugged), the recording ends there, what was captured lands, and the note gives the reason followed by "What was captured was added." If the camera hadn't settled at its frame rate when recording began, the note says what rate it ran at.

### A camera beside the screen

Choose a display or **Window…** in **Source**, tick **Record the camera too**, then choose the camera in **Camera** and its size and frame rate in **Format**. Frame Job records the screen and the camera at the same time, for a talking head over a screencast:

- **System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size**, **Include Frame Job windows** and **Rate** stay live and apply to the screen. The note under Size describes the screen.
- The camera starts as soon as the box is ticked, and the **Preview** under Format shows its live picture, so it has settled at its frame rate by the time recording begins. Unticking the box, choosing **Microphone Only**, or closing the panel turns it off.
- With no camera connected, Record says "No camera is connected."
- Pressing Record checks the Screen Recording permission, then the Camera permission, then the Microphone permission when one is chosen, then counts down.
- The panel leaves the screen as for any screen recording, and the menu-bar item is its only control.

The recording lands as `record_screen` with `camera` lands it (see [For agents](#for-agents-record_screen)): each stretch's camera movie, named after its screen movie with ` (Camera)` added, goes on one new track named **Camera** in front of everything, in the bottom-right corner, lined up with the screen. If a tool records a camera beside the screen while the panel is up, the panel's **Preview** reads "The camera is recording." until it ends.

### Microphone Only (voice-over)

See [Voice-overs](#voice-overs-microphone-only) below.

## Recording

1. Set up the panel and press **Record**.
2. Frame Job checks the permissions it needs (see [Permissions](#permissions)).
3. A **3, 2, 1** countdown appears in the panel. During the countdown the Record button reads **Cancel**, and the microphone meter already moves so you can check your level. Click **Cancel** or close the panel to stop the countdown. Nothing is recorded.
4. The recording starts and the panel leaves the screen. With **Source** set to **Camera** or **Microphone Only**, the panel stays up instead.

While the recording starts, the button reads **Starting…**. If the recording hasn't started within 20 seconds, the panel says "The recording did not start within 20 s." and goes back to idle. A Stop pressed while the button reads **Starting…** (for example **File ▸ Stop Recording**) abandons the recording, and the note reads "Stopped before the recording began; nothing was recorded."

Only one recording runs at a time. Pressing Record while another recording runs or is paused, including one an agent started, is refused with "A recording is already in progress."

### The menu-bar item

While a recording runs, Frame Job puts an item in the menu bar: a coral **●** and the elapsed time (`m:ss`, or `h:mm:ss` past an hour). Click it for its menu.

| State | Menu bar shows | Menu |
|---|---|---|
| Recording | ● and the running time | **Pause Recording**, **Stop Recording** |
| Paused | ❚❚ and the time, held still | **Resume Recording**, **Stop Recording** |

The item keeps one fixed width, so the other menu-bar items don't shift as the seconds tick. It comes down as soon as the recording stops.

### Pausing and stopping

You can pause, resume and stop from any of these places:

- the menu-bar item's menu
- **File ▸ Pause Recording**, directly under New Recording…, which reads **Resume Recording** while paused and works only while a recording runs (it has no shortcut)
- **File ▸ Stop Recording** (⌥⌘N). While any recording runs, including a paused one, **File ▸ New Recording…** reads **Stop Recording** and stops it.

The welcome window's **New Recording…** button never stops a recording. During a screen recording it only beeps, so use **File ▸ Stop Recording** or the menu-bar item. During a camera recording or a voice-over it shows the panel again.

macOS's own screen-recording indicator in the menu bar can also stop the recording. Frame Job keeps what was captured and adds it.

If you choose **Quit Frame Job** (⌘Q) during a recording, Frame Job doesn't quit. Instead it opens the menu-bar item's menu so you can stop or resume first. For a camera recording or a voice-over, it shows the panel instead.

### Paused recordings are stretches

A pause ends the current file and a resume starts a new one, so a paused recording is several files, one for each stretch between a start or resume and a pause or the stop. Each file is named by the time its stretch began. When the recording lands, the stretches sit end to end on one track, touching, with no transition between them. Each stretch's microphone file goes on the Microphone track, lined up with its own picture.

The paused time is in no file. The elapsed time counts only what was recorded.

## Where it lands

When you stop, the panel's button reads **Stopping…** and then **Adding…** while the files are written and imported.

### Into an open project

The recording goes into the project you chose in **Record Into**, at its playhead, in whatever container is open (inside a nest if you're working in one):

- The picture goes on the front track if it fits there. If not, Frame Job adds a new track in front of everything.
- The microphone goes on a new back track named **Microphone**.
- Everything is one undo step, **Add Recording**. Undo removes the clips and media entries but leaves the files on disk, just as undoing Add Media… does.
- The new clips are selected.

toolu_01FfLsikSS3yuisZLdL8unV9.prompt: Summarize Tella's positioning and feature list: recording, auto zoom, layouts, backgrounds, AI agent, MCP, transcript editing, captions, translations, sharing/hosting, publishing, pricing.

content.content:
**Positioning:** Tella is an all-in-one video creation platform for recording, editing, and sharing videos. It positions itself as a replacement for several separate tools (video messaging, product demos, long-form editing, and video hosting) and as a more customizable alternative to Loom.

**Feature list:**

- **Recording:** Integrated screen, camera, and audio recording through a web recorder, native macOS and Windows apps, and a Chrome extension. Screen and camera are captured as separate tracks, and an Auto Capture feature is listed as new.
- **Auto zoom:** Listed as "Zoom effects" in the editor.
- **Layouts:** Dynamic layouts and a layout picker, plus the ability to resize or hide the camera after recording.
- **Backgrounds:** Not mentioned on the page.
- **AI agent:** A "video agent" that can edit videos, clip them, and publish them.
- **MCP:** An MCP server integration, with a developer section.
- **Transcript editing:** Edit video through a transcript editor.
- **Captions:** Mentioned as an editing feature, alongside sound cleanup.
- **Translations:** Not mentioned on the page.
- **Sharing and hosting:** Shareable links, embedding, password protection, and videos that never expire. Clips can be up to 6 hours long.
- **Publishing:** Direct publishing to platforms such as YouTube, X, Skool, and Circle, plus export up to 4K at 60 FPS.
- **Additional tools:** Viewer analytics, team collaboration, and a shared video library.
- **Security:** SOC 2 Type II compliant.

**Pricing:** Every account starts with a 7-day free trial of the Pro plan, with no credit card required. Paid plans start at $13 per month.

## Features

**Auto zoom and cursor**
- Auto zoom follows clicks and typing, with no manual keyframing.
- Cursor styles, click animations, and click sounds, with a preview option.
- Mouse-movement tracking and cursor highlighting.
- Spotlight to highlight areas of interest.

**3D motion:** Adds tilt and perspective that follow the cursor.

**Camera**
- Records webcam, screen, or both at once.
- Dynamic layouts such as picture-in-picture and full screen, with switching during the video.
- Camera beautification (skin smoothing and brightening).

**Backgrounds:** AI background blur or replacement, applied in post-production without a green screen.

**Captions and subtitles**
- AI subtitle generation, with speech recognition in 50+ languages and a claimed accuracy above 98%.
- Subtitle editing: styling, text and timing fixes, splitting or merging blocks, and SRT import.
- The page does not mention AI translation.

**AI voice and audio**
- AI voice enhancement, AI noise reduction, and AI removal of filler words and silence.
- Background music from presets or imported audio.

**Other editing features**
- AI virtual avatar, so you can appear without showing your face.
- Annotation suite: text, shapes, arrows, callouts, and blur.
- Keyboard shortcut capture, smart pacing (typing sections sped up), and motion blur.
- Built-in teleprompter, custom watermarks, and saved presets.
- Local video import.

**Export and sharing**
- Video or GIF output, up to 4K 60fps.
- One-click aspect-ratio resizing for TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, and Twitter, so one recording can serve several platforms.
- Shareable online links with password and permission controls.

**Not found on the page:** device frames and vertical-format presets (vertical output is implied only through the social-platform resizing).

## Pricing

- No specific prices are listed; the site links to a "See Pricing" page.
- A free trial lets you explore standard features and export one video up to 4K.
- Some advanced AI features require a subscription and credits.
- A 60-day money-back guarantee applies.

## Platforms

- Windows and macOS.
- Mobile recording of iOS and Android screens via USB connection to a computer.

input.prompt: Summarize: date, what changed in Screen Studio licensing, user reaction.

toolu_01BoQFU9QLErwiDA4J5QYXhk.prompt: Summarize: date, what changed in Screen Studio licensing, user reaction.

content.content:
**Release date:** December 17, 2024

**Screen Studio 3.0 features:**
- Instant sharing through shareable links
- Custom cursors and click effects to highlight screen areas
- Dynamic camera layouts for more creative intros, plus the option to hide the camera during certain segments
- A quick share widget for sharing videos that don't need editing
- Typing detection that suggests speeding up typing segments
- A command menu with keyboard shortcuts
- Simultaneous export of multiple projects
- Bug fixes and other improvements

**Date:** October 1, 2025

**Licensing change:** Screen Studio removed its $229 lifetime license, which included one year of updates, for new purchasers. New users must now choose a subscription tier. Existing license holders get up to two years of free updates, through September 25, 2027. After that, they can keep using their current version indefinitely and can buy a renewal for further updates without being moved to a subscription.

**User reaction:** Some users called the change "misleading." Others suggested alternatives, including Screen Sage (built in Swift), the open-source apps Cap and Screenity, and Canvid, which still offers a lifetime license. Founder Adam said the email about the change was meant only for license owners and should have said more clearly that renewals remain available after 2027. He also said the $229 tier was a mistake with low adoption, and that the company, a bootstrapped team of five with no VC funding, relies on subscriptions to stay sustainable.

#

OpenScreen

OpenScreen is your free, open-source alternative to Screen Studio.

If you don't want to pay $29/month for Screen Studio but want a version that does what most people seem to need - quick, polished product demos and walkthroughs you'd post on X, Reddit or Youtube. OpenScreen does not offer every Screen Studio feature, but covers a lot of the core functionality. Screen Studio is an awesome product and this is definitely not a 1:1 clone. If you just want something fully free and open source, this project should cover most of your needs. **100% free** for both **personal** and **commercial** use. Use it, modify it, distribute it. Please respect the License. > [!NOTE] >Software should be accessible. OpenScreen has no paid tiers, premium features, upsells, or functionality locked behind a paywall. > [!WARNING] > This started as a side project that blew up; not production grade and you'll hit bugs, but hopefully it covers what you need.

## Core Features - Record a specific window, or your whole screen. - Record microphone and system audio. - Webcam overlay with picture-in-picture, drag-to-position, mirroring, and shape options. - Auto or manual zooms with adjustable depth, duration, easing, and pixel-precise position; auto-zoom follows your cursor as you work. - Custom cursor size, smoothing, and click effects, with cursor themes and post-recording path smoothing. - Automatic captions for voiceovers, generated on-device with no upload (works offline). - Wallpapers, solid colors, gradients, or your own background image. - Motion blur. - Crop, trim, and per-segment speed control on the timeline. - Text, arrow, and image annotations, with text animation presets. - Timeline snapping guides and an audio waveform to make trimming easier. - Customizable keyboard shortcuts. - Export to MP4 or GIF in multiple aspect ratios and resolutions. - Languages supported: Arabic, English, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Turkish, Vietnamese, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese. ## Installation Download the latest installer for your platform from the [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/siddharthvaddem/openscreen/releases) page. ### macOS The easiest way to install on macOS is via [Homebrew](https://brew.sh): ```bash brew install --cask siddharthvaddem/openscreen/openscreen ``` Brew automatically picks the right build for Apple Silicon or Intel, and verifies the download against a notarized signature so Gatekeeper won't block it. To update later: `brew upgrade --cask openscreen` To uninstall: `brew uninstall --cask openscreen` (add `--zap` to also remove app data) #### Manual install (if you prefer) If you'd rather grab the `.dmg` directly from the [Releases page](https://github.com/siddharthvaddem/openscreen/releases) and encounter Gatekeeper blocking the app, you can bypass it by running the following command in your terminal after installation: ```bash xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Openscreen.app

input.prompt: List Screen Studio news items with dates, especially anything after 4.0 (sensitive data auto-masking, face masking, Finder preview, new export engine, rollbacks of audio features).

toolu_01HmJ1C2jmtYBRZB2Z7jxZGj.prompt: List Screen Studio news items with dates, especially anything after 4.0 (sensitive data auto-masking, face masking, Finder preview, new export engine, rollbacks of audio features).

content.content:
**Plans and prices**

- **Lifetime:** $39, one payment. Includes 5 GB of shared recordings, each kept for 3 months after upload.
- **Pro:** $9 per month, billed monthly. Includes unlimited shared recordings for as long as the subscription is active.
- Both plans run the same app and export the same file. The only difference is online storage for shareable links.
- There is no free plan and no yearly plan.
- The lifetime price was $29 at launch and is now $39.

**Trial terms**

- Both plans include a 7-day free trial of the full app, with no watermark and no length limit.
- Videos exported during the trial are yours and keep working afterward, whether or not you pay.

**License**

- The page describes the Lifetime option as a "licence you have already bought," with "no renewal and nothing to cancel."
- It does not say whether Prequel is source-available, open source, or under any named license, so I can't confirm that from this page.

The page doesn't include any Screen Studio news items, dates, or version history. It doesn't mention 4.0, sensitive data auto-masking, face masking, Finder preview, the new export engine, or audio feature rollbacks.

The only dates are the affiliate terms' "Checked 2026-10-10" note and the copyright year, neither of which is news. The page describes Screen Studio as a Mac-only screen recorder with Auto Zoom, Smooth Cursor, and Backgrounds features. For release history, check the official Screen Studio site or the Creators Toolbox News section.

input.prompt: How does Screen Studio handle the cursor: is it recorded separately from the video? List cursor options (size, smoothing, hide when idle, loop, styles, click effects, motion blur) and any requirements.

toolu_014eKRK5p8Y4mb3k5nB5uqFT.prompt: How does Screen Studio handle the cursor: is it recorded separately from the video? List cursor options (size, smoothing, hide when idle, loop, styles, click effects, motion blur) and any requirements.

input.prompt: How does automatic zoom work: what triggers zooms (clicks, typing), what can be edited, any settings, and what recordings it requires.

toolu_019vpxJzpQHMV6SXe8ZSko97.prompt: How does automatic zoom work: what triggers zooms (clicks, typing), what can be edited, any settings, and what recordings it requires.

content.content:
Auto zoom is triggered by mouse clicks. It "focuses on the areas where clicks occurred during your recording" and detects the click positions to zoom in on them.

- **Triggers:** Clicks only. The page doesn't mention typing or other input.
- **Editing:** Each zoom can be set to Auto or Manual. For Manual, you select the area yourself. The page doesn't describe other editing options.
- **Settings:** None are listed on this page.
- **Recording requirements:** The recording must contain mouse clicks. Auto zoom added where no click occurs won't zoom to any area.

**Separate recording:** The page doesn't say whether the cursor is captured separately from the video. It only says that "Hide cursor" removes it from the recording.

**Cursor options (Cursor Settings):**
- **Size:** adjusts how visible or subtle the cursor is.
- **Hide cursor:** removes the cursor entirely.
- **Hide when idle:** hides the cursor when it isn't moving.
- **Loop cursor position:** moves the cursor back to its starting point near the end, for a seamless loop.
- **Styles:** macOS or Touch. The Touch style is mostly used for iPad and iPhone recordings.
- **Always use default system cursor:** keeps the system cursor from changing during actions like text selection.

**Advanced options:**
- **Rotate cursor while moving:** slightly tilts the cursor to mimic chasing the mouse.
- **Remove cursor shakes:** reduces unintended movement, often from accessibility tools.
- **Stop cursor movement at the end:** halts the cursor before the video ends.
- **Optimize original cursor types:** reduces rapid cursor-type changes.

**Not covered on this page:**
- **Smoothing:** a separate guide, "Disable smooth mouse movement," is listed in the navigation, but its contents aren't included.
- **Click effects** and **motion blur:** not mentioned.

**Requirements:** The page says some features depend on your Mac and macOS version, but it doesn't specify which cursor features that applies to.

input.segment: Screen-recording and tutorial / product-demo video tools, as of 2026-11-01: Screen Studio-style "polished screencast" recorders (Screen Studio, Cap, FocuSee, Prequel, ScreenKite, OpenScreen), all-in-one record-edit-host tools (Tella, Loom), long-standing screencast NLEs (Camtasia, ScreenFlow), device-mockup tools (Rotato, Screenhance), and AI product-video makers (Arcade, Clueso, Trupeer, Supademo). Method: vendor changelogs, help pages and official blogs first. Competitor blogs (Prequel, ScreenKite, Tella) and review aggregators are used only for corroboration and user sentiment, and are marked where used. I did not run any product. FRAME JOB'S BASELINE, from /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/docs/guide/screen-recording.md: the pointer and click rings are burned into the recorded picture, and no cursor, click or keystroke events are stored. The camera beside the screen is fixed in the bottom-right corner with no shape or layout control. The guide says "There's no keystroke or callout overlay". There is no camera background removal (issue #124, E9 Remove Background through Vision, is deferred). There are no share links. Zoom to Region (Z) is manual. On the other side, Frame Job already has a real multi-track NLE, grading and LUTs, HDR, a pro audio chain, filler and silence removal, motion graphics including keycaps and window frames, AV1/VP9 export, and the whole editor over local MCP plus an in-app Assistant.

tools.name: Screen Studio
tools.positioning: The tool that defined the category: a Mac-only recorder with a light editor that makes a raw screen recording look 'produced' with no editing skill (auto zoom, smooth cursor, backgrounds). Made by a bootstrapped team of five. Subscription-only since October 2025.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Praise: a polished result in minutes with near-zero editing, and auto zoom that 'just works' from clicks. Reviewers call the app quality 'unquestionable'. Complaints: subscription-only pricing ($29/mo or $108/yr; the $229 lifetime licence was withdrawn 2025-10-01 and users called the change 'misleading'). It is Mac-only, share links stop at 30 minutes, there is no team plan, and export is capped at 4K60. 4.0 shipped with regressions: export failures and stalls, a black editor on Intel/AMD Macs, and audio-enhancement features temporarily rolled back to beta on 2026-10-09. Those reports come from a competitor's blog (ScreenKite) quoting the vendor's Telegram group and X, so they are unverified.

headline_features.detail: Zooms toward the clicks captured during recording. The help page says clicks are the only trigger. Manual zooms are also auto-animated. 'Smart framing' places zooms so the webcam never covers the cursor, and vertical exports re-aim every zoom.
'Focuses on the areas where clicks occurred during your recording'. Each zoom can be Auto or Manual. A zoom placed where no click happened has nothing to aim at.

Smooth cursor (turns shaky paths into a glide), size, hide, hide when idle, loop cursor to its start for seamless loops, macOS or Touch style, rotate while moving, remove cursor shakes, stop movement at the end, sharp system cursors, click effects (circle or ripple), and click sounds.
'Optics-based' blur on fast cursor and zoom movement.
macOS wallpapers, gradients, your own image or Unsplash photos, with adjustable shadow angle, distance and softness, plus padding and inset. Presets can be saved and shared with a team.

Layouts: Fullscreen camera, Split screen, Camera overlay, Screen only and Camera cutout, with animated transitions between them. Camera cutout removes the background on-device with no green screen (beta). Also face tracking, 'Hide during silence', 12 camera looks, LUT import, crop and sharpen.

headline_features.feature: Glass Loupe and an on-device upscaler
headline_features.detail: A lens magnifies one area while the rest of the screen stays visible. A local AI model ('6.5× upscale') sharpens zoomed-in text.

headline_features.feature: Edit by transcript, plus filler words and pauses
headline_features.detail: Deleting a transcript sentence cuts the video. One pass shortens filler words and long pauses. On-device transcription, with cloud transcription optional. The edited transcript exports as SRT.
On-device transcription with styled, animated captions (font, colour, position, timing, animation).

headline_features.feature: Keystroke overlay ('Show shortcuts') and speeding up typing
headline_features.detail: Shows the keys pressed on screen. Typing detection (since 3.0) suggests speeding up typing stretches.
16:9, 1:1 and 9:16 with zooms, layouts and captions re-adjusted automatically. Reel mode overlays the Instagram or TikTok interface so you can check nothing is hidden behind it.

headline_features.feature: iPhone and iPad recording with device frames
headline_features.detail: Records over USB with a matching device mockup and nothing installed on the device. 3.5.2 (January 2026) added an iPhone 17 Pro Max frame.
Covers API keys or emails after recording. Highlight dims the rest of the frame. Automatic detection of such data after 4.0 is reported by a third party but not confirmed on a primary page.
On-device voice modes (Standard, Noise reduction, Podcast (beta)), background music, and AI voiceover from typed text, which sends the text to the cloud.

Links at 1080p60 for videos up to 30 minutes, with comments, private links and view counts. Editable projects up to 20 GB can be shared by link (beta in 4.0). Copy the finished video to the clipboard.

Resize the recorded window to an exact size, hide desktop icons, speaker notes, countdown, pause and resume, one global shortcut, and crash recovery that saves every 2 s. Built on ScreenCaptureKit. Export uses the media-engine hardware encoder (MP4 at 720p, 1080p or 4K up to 60 fps, or GIF).

tools.name: Camtasia (TechSmith: Camtasia Editor + Rev + Audiate + Camtasia Online)
tools.positioning: A veteran Windows and Mac screencast NLE for training and L&D teams. Renamed 'Camtasia Editor' on 2026-02-04 inside a 'Camtasia suite': Rev is a quick-layout recorder workflow, Audiate does text-based audio editing and AI voices, and Camtasia Online handles browser collaboration.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Praise: a deep timeline with callouts, annotations, quizzes and assets, the most manual control in the segment, a mature cursor toolkit, and fit for training teams. Complaints: a steep learning curve (42 G2 reviews mention it), subscription-only since the 2025 version, a high price for individuals (Essentials from $179.88/yr), resource-heavy with crashes on complex projects, audio-sync problems, licence server checks, and no built-in hosting (every share is an export plus an upload). G2 rates it 4.6/5 from 1,756 reviews.

headline_features.detail: Automatic zoom and pan for Rev media, made a screen effect in 2026.0.0. It analyses the recording to follow the cursor or the active window.

headline_features.feature: Rev quick layouts, looks and vertical
headline_features.detail: Rev picks size, layout, background, effects and filters in one step. Rev media can be adjusted on the canvas (2026.0.0). Vertical-aspect Looks and Layouts arrived in 2026.1.0.

Cursor smoothing (Camtasia recordings only), cursor path editing, the Cursor Path Creator for footage recorded elsewhere, scaling, replacing the pointer with a logo, glow, magnify, click effects, motion blur, and cursor elevation 'Always on Top' (its default became a setting in 2026.2.4).
Sends media to Camtasia Audiate (a separate product) for text-based editing, filler and hesitation removal, and audio clean-up.

AI voices, AI avatars, AI translation of audio and transcripts (7 languages, 9 dialects), AI script writing, AI image creator, AI titles, descriptions and chapters (in Screencast), and generative AI video. The features page is undated.
Social-style captions, applied directly to Rev media since 2026.0.0. Basic VTT import and export in 2026.1.0.
Removes the webcam background without a green screen and replaces it with an image or a dynamic background.

headline_features.feature: Snagit steps to a training video
headline_features.detail: Step-by-step screenshots from Snagit 2026.3+ become a ready-to-share training video automatically (2026.2.0).

headline_features.feature: Sync by audio, Zoom import, WebM export and SVG
headline_features.detail: Sync media timing by audio and import Zoom cloud recordings (2026.1.0). WebM export and Lottie-backed animated assets (2026.2.0). SVG Tiny 1.2 (2026.2.2).
A browser recorder and collaboration workflow, launched from the Home window from 2026.0.4. Third-party reviews say real-time multi-editor collaboration is still missing.

tools.name: ScreenFlow (Telestream)
tools.positioning: A long-standing Mac screencast editor with a perpetual-licence feel. It has been effectively in maintenance mode since its 2025 recording update.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Picked for a traditional record-and-edit timeline on the Mac with no account. The signal against it: no auto zoom, no AI captions and no transcript editing in any 2024–2026 release. The last feature release was 10.5 (2025-08-04), and 10.5.2 (2026-02-12) was fixes only. It is falling behind the Screen Studio-style tools.

headline_features.detail: Exclude ScreenFlow or specific apps, record a region, looped and timed recordings, native system audio with per-app audio and no driver, and a Recording Monitor preview with levels.

headline_features.feature: Background removal filter and cursor smoothing
headline_features.detail: An ML background-removal filter and cursor smoothing, both from 10.0 (2021). Nothing newer in this area.
10.5.2, with fixes for macOS 26.2 crashes and chroma-key export. No auto zoom or AI features are listed.

tools.name: Tella
tools.positioning: A cloud record-edit-host-publish platform for demos, tutorials, courses and async video (Mac, Windows, web, Chrome). By late 2026 it is the most agent-forward tool in the segment: a public API and MCP, Claude Code skills, an in-editor Tella Agent, and Tella Motion.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Praise: one place to record, edit (transcript, layouts, zooms), host with analytics, and publish straight to YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, LinkedIn and X. It ships weekly. Complaints and limits: no free plan (7-day trial, Pro from $13/user/mo), agent messages cost credits, Auto Capture cannot record localhost or desktop apps, and it is not built for frame-level or VFX editing (its own blog says so). Everything is cloud-hosted.

headline_features.feature: Auto zoom from clicks and cursor
headline_features.detail: Auto Zoom has existed since 2024-09-24 (Mac app). Auto Zooms V2 came 2025-09-24. Adaptive zooms became the default 2026-08-21, zooms auto-apply after recording since 2026-09-04, punch-in zooms arrived 2026-10-09, and presets (Subtle, Moderate, Focused, Intense) on 2026-10-23.

headline_features.feature: Effect panel: cursor, motion blur, highlights, blurs
headline_features.detail: One panel for zooms, animated cursors, blurs and highlights, with motion blur and cursor styling (2026-09-10). Animated cursor controls arrived 2026-08-28.

Multi-layouts and transitions since 2023–24, Auto Layouts (2025-07-10), Custom Layouts (2025-11-20), Vertical 50/50, Perspective layout, and Cut out camera background removal (2026-09-18). Also pop-out camera frames, the Blob camera style, animated borders, colour filters and LUTs (2026-09-25), and eye-contact correction (2026-10-09).
Text-based editing since 2024-05-02. Auto Cut (2025-07-22) finds mistakes, repeated lines and interruptions and removes them in one click. Silence detection combines amplitude with VAD (2026-05-22).

The API and MCP launched 2025-12-18. Clip API with cuts, zooms, blurs and layouts as MCP tools (2026-05-08). Batched apply_video_edits (2026-08-21). Storyboards (2026-09-04). Listed in Claude's Connector Directory (2026-08-06). An MCP settings page covers ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor and Codex (2026-07-24).
Open-source video workflows built for Claude Code, including local file editing and YouTube publishing.

Edits from a text description: cuts, zooms and layouts appear live and can be undone. It asks clarifying questions, makes 9:16 clips, and fills gaps with generated b-roll, sound effects or Motion graphics. Can use your own ChatGPT or Claude plan. It 'does not invent what you said or add narration'. Paid credits (4,500 a month per Pro seat).
An agent builds animated titles, charts, diagrams, lower thirds and b-roll on a keyframe and easing engine. There is no keyframe timeline for the user.
An AI records a walkthrough of a web page on Tella's servers at 4K60, started by Tella Agent or any MCP agent. It cannot record localhost, desktop or mobile apps.

Publish directly to YouTube, Shorts, LinkedIn, X and TikTok, with subtitle translations (2026-09-30). Instagram and Facebook added 2026-10-30. Scheduled publishing came 2026-10-16. Social safe zones for portrait (2026-05-22).
Hosted pages with analytics, comments, password protection, custom domains and embeds. Real-time co-editing in the new editor (2026-09-18).

tools.name: Loom (Atlassian)
tools.positioning: Async work video for teams, and in 2026 increasingly 'record for agents'. It is not a polish or screencast-effects tool.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Praise: the fastest record-and-share link, strong hosting, and a G2 rating of 4.7/5 from 2,349 reviews. Complaints: Trustpilot 1.4/5 from 204 reviews, login trouble after the Atlassian migration, seat-band price jumps, Business going from $18 to $20 (2026-06-05, per a third-party tracker), AI locked to Business + AI (about $24/user/mo), a 5-minute cap on the free plan, and no auto zoom.

headline_features.detail: A native rebuild for macOS 15+ that is about 80% smaller. Camera bubbles in circle, squircle, portrait or landscape that snap to the edges. Filters and custom backgrounds, a teleprompter below the camera, and automatic decluttering that hides desktop icons, the menu bar, tabs and notifications.

headline_features.feature: Record for agent and video prompts
headline_features.detail: Turns a narrated screen recording (transcript, click screenshots, links) into a step-by-step action plan or prompt for agents (Rovo, Claude, coding assistants), or into a Jira item. Magic Pen and a Selection tool mark UI elements. Business + AI and Enterprise plans only.
Agents (Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Codex) can pull transcripts, metadata and action items, add timestamped comments, and share or organise recordings. They cannot edit the video.

headline_features.feature: Edit by transcript, plus filler-word and silence removal
headline_features.detail: Trim by selecting words in the transcript. Toggles for Remove filler words and Remove Silence. Business + AI plan.
Loom AI generates titles, summaries and chapters, and runs workflows.

tools.name: Cap (cap.so)
tools.positioning: An open-source Loom and Screen Studio alternative for Mac and Windows: Studio Mode for polished local edits and Instant Mode for share links. Core code is AGPLv3 (the cap-camera* and scap-* crates are MIT). About 24.2k GitHub stars. Ships several times a week. Moved to a native GPUI app in 0.6.1.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Praise: free for personal use, a $58 lifetime desktop licence, open source and self-hostable, custom S3 or Google Drive storage, near-identical Mac and Windows apps, and very fast iteration. Complaints: a younger product with a smaller editing set (per Tella's comparison), free share links capped at 5 minutes, self-hosting falls on you, and some confusion about pricing. Licence note for Frame Job (Apache-2.0): Cap's AGPL code cannot be carried over, the same rule as Concat.

headline_features.detail: Experimental from 0.3.62 (2025-08-06). Spring-based zoom with cursor and display motion blur in 0.5.4 (2026-07-06). Keeps a resting cursor in view, ignores cursor movement in cut sections, and works on multi-take timelines (0.6.1 and 0.6.2).

Custom cursor capture on by default (0.3.67). High-resolution SVG cursors. Hide an inactive cursor with a fade (0.3.74). Smooth and Fast cursor presets, and a cursor-only ProRes 4444 export (0.4.82). Cursor styles with click ripples (0.6.0). Smoothed cursors settle where the mouse stopped (0.6.2).
3D tracks give automatic or custom camera shots with perspective, easing and focus blur. Style tracks change the background, camera or cursor for one section only.
Blur or remove the camera background on macOS, in preview and export (0.6.0). Better removal that keeps only the main person (0.6.1).

headline_features.feature: Keyboard press overlay track and caption tracks
headline_features.detail: A keyboard-press overlay track and caption tracks in the timeline (0.4.81). Local Whisper and Parakeet transcription. Caption presets and animations with SRT and VTT export (0.5.3).
A word-level transcript editor (0.4.82, 0.5.3).

headline_features.feature: Cap for agents: CLI, skill and local MCP server
headline_features.detail: Agents (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor) can record, export, upload and share, and read transcripts, AI summaries, chapters, comments and analytics, with JSON output and confirmation before changes. The notes do NOT say agents can edit the timeline (zooms or cuts).
Built-in teleprompter, clip transitions, and blur and pixelate masks (0.5.7). Scenes with split screen (0.5.1). Decorative frames (0.5.4). Animated gradient backgrounds and Studio Sound (0.6.0).
9:16 area and window presets, and portrait videos fill vertical projects (0.6.2). Image backgrounds are re-cropped when the aspect ratio changes (0.6.1).

Free for personal use (4K60 export, 5-minute links). Desktop $29/yr or $58 lifetime (commercial use, 20 links a month). Pro $12/user/mo ($8.16 billed annually) with unlimited links, AI titles, summaries and chapters, custom domain, password-protected shares, viewer analytics, and custom S3 or Google Drive storage. Self-hosting keeps all features.

tools.name: FocuSee (iMobie)
tools.positioning: A Windows and Mac Screen Studio-style recorder with auto zoom, cursor effects, an AI avatar and a beauty filter. Sold as an annual licence or a lifetime licence.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Picked as the Windows option for Screen Studio-style output, with a lifetime licence ($199.99, or from $49.99/yr per Tella's comparison). Weaknesses: hosting is a paid add-on, there is no team workspace, and advanced AI features need credits.

headline_features.feature: Auto zoom from clicks and typing
headline_features.detail: Auto typing recognition generates zooms from typing (2.4.0 Mac, 2026-07-16; improved in 2.4.1). Smart speed-up of typing sections.
Custom cursor angle, dynamic direction, idle duration, path smoothness, and end position (2.5.0).

headline_features.feature: 3D motion, spotlight, motion blur and keyboard shortcut capture
headline_features.detail: Tilt and perspective that follow the cursor, cursor highlighting, spotlight, motion blur, and keyboard shortcut capture.
PiP and full-screen layouts that switch mid-video, AI background blur or replacement in post, a beauty filter, and custom layout presets (2.5.0).

headline_features.feature: AI subtitles, AI avatar, teleprompter and audio clean-up
headline_features.detail: Subtitles in 50+ languages with SRT import. An AI virtual avatar so you can appear without your face. Teleprompter. Voice enhancement, noise reduction, and filler and silence removal.

headline_features.feature: Resizing for social platforms and share links
headline_features.detail: One-click aspect-ratio resizing for TikTok, YouTube, Instagram and others. Full-screen support for vertical video (2.3.5 Windows). Share links with password and permissions.

tools.name: Prequel (prequel.sh) — new entrant
tools.positioning: A 'cinematic' Mac screen recorder that 'does the editing for you', aimed straight at Screen Studio 4. Launched on Product Hunt 2026-08-30 (198 upvotes, #4 of the day). Ships almost daily. Apple Silicon and macOS 14+ only. All processing is local.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Pitched on price ($39 lifetime or $9/mo, the same app on both) and on matching Screen Studio 4 features within weeks of it. Thin independent feedback so far: one Product Hunt review at 4/5, and a commenter who wanted a lifetime option, which was added at launch. Its own comparison posts are marketing.

headline_features.feature: Auto zoom from clicks and typing, with 3D tilt and yaw
headline_features.detail: Zooms target the cursor, a drawn region, or the field being typed into (typing needs the Accessibility permission). Level, speed, tilt, yaw and blur falloff are set per zoom. Each zoom is an ordinary timeline slice.
A Loupe zoom method (v0.0.35, 2026-10-02) with light spill (v0.1.1). Fisheye zoom (v0.7.0, 2026-10-21).

The pointer is stored as data, not burned into the picture (v0.0.26). Fifteen pointer styles, resized to stay visible during zooms, smoothed while moving, hidden after stillness, and motion-blurred. Click effects (ripples, confetti, chalk), plus click and typing sounds.

Fourteen layouts, switchable per clip. Camera shapes (circle, squircle, rounded, wide, portrait, 'Follow me'). Camera background removal (v0.0.19) and a cut-out layout (v0.8.1). Camera colour looks. Rotation at any angle.

headline_features.feature: Teleprompter in the notch with voice tracking
headline_features.detail: The script sits under the camera notch and highlights each word as it is spoken. It pauses when you go off script and catches up when you skip ahead.

headline_features.feature: Subtitles and edit by deleting sentences
headline_features.detail: On-device transcription. Fix a word by typing over it, or delete a sentence to cut it. Styles: Blur in, Subtitle, Highlight and Band.

headline_features.feature: CLI and a Claude Code skill
headline_features.detail: A `prequel` command-line tool and a Claude Code skill (v0.1.0).

MP4 (H.264 or HEVC) up to 4K and 120 fps, constant frame rate, VideoToolbox plus Metal. Framing is stored as proportions so a layout survives a switch to 9:16. Presets for YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, Reels, X and LinkedIn. Filters (Dream, Dither, Lost signal). Share links involve an upload.
$39 lifetime (5 GB of shared recordings kept 3 months) or $9/mo (unlimited sharing). A 7-day trial with no watermark.

tools.name: ScreenKite — new entrant
tools.positioning: A free native Mac recorder and editor (exports watermarked until Pro) whose pitch is that a local AI agent edits the recording with the same tools the UI uses. Pro is $79.99 one-time for 3 Macs, rising to $99.99 after 2026-10-31. It also publishes aggressive blog posts against Screen Studio.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Picked by creators who already pay for Claude Code or Codex and want agent editing with no extra AI fee, plus a one-time price. Every source is the vendor's own marketing (version 1.18, September 2026), so treat it as unverified. This is the closest competitor to Frame Job's MCP and Assistant model.

headline_features.detail: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Grok Build and Kimi drive the same editing tools as the UI. Meaning-changing edits return a plan with confirm:false and apply with confirm:true. Edits undo like clicks. There is a CLI (`screenkite agent export --json`). MCP is not stated.

headline_features.feature: Auto zoom, transcript cutting and on-device captions
headline_features.detail: Auto zoom on clicks and keystrokes, transcript-based cutting, and on-device captions with WhisperKit (Apple Silicon; Intel falls back to ElevenLabs cloud). Backgrounds, padding, rounded corners and shadows. Export up to 1080p60 H.264.

tools.name: OpenScreen (open source)
tools.positioning: 'Your free, open-source alternative to Screen Studio' (MIT). About 40k GitHub stars, which is the strongest adoption signal for a free Screen Studio-style tool. Archived after v1.5.0 (2026-06-06), with a community continuation at getopenscreen/openscreen.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Free with no paid tiers, and free for commercial use. The author warns it is 'not production grade and you'll hit bugs'. Its star count shows how much demand there is for a non-subscription, open polished-screencast tool.

headline_features.detail: Window or screen recording with mic and system audio. Webcam PiP with shapes. Auto or manual zooms that follow the cursor.
