Cursor size, smoothing, click effects and post-recording path smoothing. On-device captions. Wallpaper and gradient backgrounds. Motion blur. Crop, trim and speed. Annotations. MP4 or GIF in several aspect ratios.

tools.name: Rotato (and Screenhance) — device mockups
tools.positioning: 3D device-mockup renderers for app launch videos and store assets, alongside screen recorders rather than replacing them.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Rotato gives freely directed 3D (camera, lighting, depth of field) on 30+ hand-built devices, a one-time Mac licence, and offline rendering. The criticism: animation is template-driven rather than keyframed (Screenhance's comparison), and the licence does not cover every future update. Screenhance offers preset 3D device templates plus screen-recording 'Studio' and store-set automation, with less freedom than Rotato.

headline_features.detail: Phones, tablets, laptops and desktops. Timeline-based camera and device animation, reflections, shadows, depth of field, clay styles. Renders up to 8K. Exports H.264 and HEVC, transparent HEVC with alpha or ProRes 4444, image sequences, and Lottie. iPhone mirroring and USB screen recording. A Figma plugin.
Device turns, laptop lid openings, floating arcs and an iPhone Duo fold, plus App Store screenshot sets.

tools.name: Arcade (arcade.software) — AI product video
tools.positioning: Began as interactive product demos and is now an AI product-video generator: you describe the video, and an agent writes the script, builds scenes, records the product and adds voiceover.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Picked for marketing and product teams who want a narrated launch or feature video without recording or narrating themselves. AI-video Pro is about $59/mo per a third-party list. A vendor benchmark claims AI voiceover lifts completion 14% (unverified).

headline_features.detail: Arcade asks questions, drafts a plan and generates after you approve (2026-05-27). Chat edits restructure scenes and change messaging (2026-06-25). The agent watches its own output and fixes visible problems (2026-09-17). Choice of model per video: Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 or Haiku 5.5, plus 3D prompts (2026-10-20).

Chrome extension recordings get a smooth cursor, highlighted clicks and automatic zooms (2026-10-20). Desktop cursor animations gained motion blur and click feedback (2026-06-10). Screen, camera and voice with switching in one take (2026-09-29).

ElevenLabs v3 with emotion control (2026-01-26). Up to three narrators (2026-09-29). Brand-kit pronunciations and editing the whole voiceover as one script (2026-08-19). An AI voice per language for translations.

tools.name: Clueso / Trupeer — AI product-video makers
tools.positioning: Turn a rough screen recording into a polished narrated product or training video: AI script rewrite, AI voiceover, auto zoom on clicks, avatars, translation, and a matching written guide.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: G2 reviewers describe going from a day of recording and editing to minutes. The criticism: AI voiceover can sound synthetic, and complex apps need manual zoom fixes. Clueso starts around $50/mo per a third-party list. Vendor pages are undated, so the 2026 state is not confirmed.

headline_features.feature: Script rewrite and synced AI voiceover (Clueso)
headline_features.detail: Transcribes your narration, polishes it into an editable script, and regenerates a synced AI voiceover. Auto zoom on clicks, removal of mistakes and dead air, callouts, branding, translation with AI voice, and a step-by-step text guide with screenshots.
Zooms added automatically on every click and action. AI voiceover in many accents (the vendor's figures conflict: 65+ and 120+). A stock or custom avatar narrator. Filler removal. Auto chapters.

tools.name: Supademo
tools.positioning: An interactive-demo builder with a growing video editor. Included only because it edits video.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Picked for clickable demos with AI voiceover. Video-side zoom is behind the others.

headline_features.feature: Video editor redesign and AI voiceover
headline_features.detail: A redesigned video editor (splitting, trimming, timeline) in February 2026. Voiceovers 2.0 with an expressive mode in June 2026. More voiceover languages in September 2026.

headline_features.feature: Video zoom and pan, and chapters
headline_features.detail: Described as 'coming next' in the September 2026 recap.

trends.trend: The cursor is captured as data, not burned into the picture, and everything Screen Studio made popular rests on that
trends.evidence: Auto zoom, cursor smoothing, resizing, hide-when-idle, restyling, click effects, looping and motion blur all require pointer position and click and key events recorded separately from the frames. Prequel made 'Pointer no longer baked into recordings' a changelog item (v0.0.26). Cap captures custom cursors by default and even exports a cursor-only ProRes 4444. Screen Studio's auto zoom 'focuses on the areas where clicks occurred during your recording'. Camtasia's cursor smoothing works only on Camtasia's own recordings for the same reason. Frame Job's recorder burns the pointer and click rings into the movie and stores no events, so none of this category's table stakes can be built until that changes.

trends.trend: Auto zoom has moved from 'zoom on clicks' to cinematic camera work: typing triggers, spring physics, motion blur, loupe and fisheye lenses, 3D perspective, and zooms that re-aim for vertical
trends.evidence: FocuSee added typing-triggered zooms (2026-07-16). Prequel aims at the field being typed into and has per-zoom tilt and yaw (2026). Cap has spring-based zoom with motion blur (2026-07-06) and 3D tracks with camera shots and focus blur (2026-08-31). Screen Studio added Glass Loupe (2026-10-02). Prequel added Loupe (2026-10-02) and fisheye (2026-10-21). Tella added punch-in zooms and intensity presets (October 2026). Screen Studio uses an on-device upscaler so zoomed text stays sharp.

trends.trend: The presenter camera gets pro treatment: cutout without a green screen, face tracking, hide-during-silence, looks and LUTs, eye contact, shapes and split layouts
trends.evidence: Screen Studio 4 (2026-10-02): camera cutout (beta), face tracking, 'Hide during silence', 12 looks plus LUTs, split screen. Cap 0.6.0 and 0.6.1: background blur and removal. Tella: Cut out (2026-09-18), LUTs (2026-09-25), eye-contact correction (2026-10-09). Prequel: cutout (2026-09-13). FocuSee: beauty filter. Loom for Mac: bubble shapes and backgrounds (2026-10-07).

trends.trend: Every recorder now ships an agent surface, but most agents only drive record, export and share, not the edit
trends.evidence: Tella: API and MCP (2025-12-18), clip-editing MCP tools (2026-05-08), Claude Code skills (2026-07-12), in-editor Tella Agent (public beta 2026-10-16/30). Cap: CLI, skill and local MCP (2026-07-20), with recording, export, sharing and transcripts but no timeline editing listed. Prequel: CLI plus a Claude Code skill (2026-10-05). ScreenKite: 83 agent editing tools with plan-then-confirm (vendor claim). Loom: Record for agent plus Atlassian MCP (2026-10-22). Arcade: a describe-to-video agent on Claude models (2026-10-20). Frame Job's whole-editor local MCP plus an in-app Assistant, with every edit an undo step, is no longer unique in kind. It is still the deepest in scope, being a full NLE.

trends.trend: Edit by transcript plus one-pass filler, pause and mistake removal has become standard in recorders, not just in Descript
trends.evidence: Screen Studio 4 (transcript editing, filler words and pauses). Cap word-level transcript editor (2026-04-02). Tella Auto Cut, which removes mistakes and repeated lines (2025-07-22). Loom (Business + AI). Prequel (delete a sentence). Camtasia via Audiate's Edit as Text.

trends.trend: Generated narration and describe-to-video in product-demo tools
trends.evidence: Arcade writes the script, builds scenes and voices them, with chat editing and an agent that checks its own output. Clueso rewrites your narration into a clean script and regenerates a synced AI voiceover. Trupeer and Camtasia/Audiate offer AI voices, avatars and translation. Screen Studio has cloud AI voiceover from typed text. Tella deliberately 'does not invent what you said or add narration'.

trends.trend: One recording, every aspect ratio, with zooms and layouts re-framed automatically, social safe zones, and direct publishing
trends.evidence: Screen Studio re-aims zooms for 9:16 and has Reel mode safe-zone overlays. Prequel stores framing as proportions. Cap added 9:16 presets and portrait fill (2026-10-28). Camtasia Rev added vertical looks (2026-04-14). Tella added social safe zones (2026-05-22) and direct publishing to YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, LinkedIn, X, Instagram and Facebook (2026-09-30 and 10-30).

trends.trend: A teleprompter built into the recorder
trends.evidence: Prequel's notch teleprompter with voice tracking (2026-09-18). Cap teleprompter (2026-07-20). Loom for Mac teleprompter (2026-10-07). FocuSee teleprompter. Screen Studio speaker notes.

trends.trend: Backlash against subscription pricing, and a wave of lifetime, free and open-source alternatives
trends.evidence: Screen Studio dropped its lifetime licence on 2025-10-01 and users called the move 'misleading'. It now charges $29/mo or $108/yr. Camtasia has been subscription-only since 2025. Alternatives: OpenScreen (MIT, about 40k stars), Cap (open source, $58 lifetime), Prequel ($39 lifetime), ScreenKite ($79.99 one-time), FocuSee ($199.99 lifetime). Frame Job is free, open source and bring-your-own-key, which is a strong position in this fight.

trends.trend: Hosted share links are how the category makes money, and bring-your-own storage is emerging
trends.evidence: Screen Studio links (30-minute cap, comments, view counts). Cap Pro links with a custom domain, analytics and custom S3 or Google Drive storage, plus full-featured self-hosting. Tella's hosted pages and analytics. Prequel links tied to plan storage. Camtasia and ScreenFlow have no hosting, which reviewers flag.

trends.trend: On-device processing and native performance as selling points, and stability as the risk
trends.evidence: Screen Studio says recording, transcripts, voice enhancement, face tracking and export are all local, with 3x faster exports in 4.0. Prequel, ScreenKite (WhisperKit) and Loom rebuilt native for Mac (2026-10-07). Cap moved from Tauri to native GPUI (0.6.1, 2026-10-20). Screen Studio 4.0's reported export failures and feature rollbacks show that reliability on long projects is still a weak point.

trends.trend: Masking sensitive on-screen data
trends.evidence: Screen Studio's sensitive-data masks for API keys and emails, plus Highlight. Cap's blur and pixelate masks (2026-07-20). Tella's blurs and highlights that work during zooms. Loom for Mac's automatic decluttering of tabs, bookmarks and notifications.

table_stakes: Recording a display, a window or a dragged area, with camera, mic and system audio as SEPARATE tracks; pause and resume, countdown, a global shortcut, and crash recovery. Frame Job has most of this, but no area capture.

Cursor and click (and increasingly keystroke) events captured alongside the video, so the pointer can be resized, restyled, smoothed, hidden when idle or removed after recording, with click highlights and click sounds. Frame Job: missing, because the pointer is burned in.

Automatic zoom from clicks (and now typing) that produces editable zoom segments on the timeline, plus manual zoom, eased or spring motion, and motion blur on zoom and pan. Frame Job has manual Zoom to Region actions only.
Background canvas around the recording: wallpapers, gradients, images, padding, rounded corners, shadow and inset. Saved and shareable style presets.

Camera overlay with shapes (circle, squircle, rounded) and layouts (PiP corner, side by side, stacked, full camera, screen only) that switch mid-video with animated transitions, placed so it never covers the cursor. Frame Job: fixed bottom-right corner.
On-device auto-captions with styled and animated presets and SRT/VTT export. Frame Job has this.
Edit by transcript plus one-click removal of filler words and silences. Frame Job has filler and silence removal; check that deleting text in a transcript view cuts the video.
Speeding up selected sections (especially typing) and trim, cut and crop.
Keystroke and shortcut overlay generated from recorded key events. Frame Job has only a manual keycap graphic.
Switching the output to 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1 with zooms, layouts and captions re-framed automatically.
Blur or pixelate masks and highlight or spotlight for sensitive or important regions. Frame Job has obscure and spotlight.
Voice clean-up (noise reduction or 'studio sound') and background music. Frame Job's audio chain is ahead of the whole segment here.
Export up to 4K60 MP4 and GIF using the hardware encoder.
Some way to share: a hosted link with comments and views, or at least copy to clipboard or direct publish. Frame Job has none.
differentiators: Camera cutout without a green screen, plus face tracking and hide-the-camera-during-silence (Screen Studio 4, Cap 0.6, Tella, Prequel). Shipped by the leaders in September–October 2026 but still beta at Screen Studio, so a well-made version still stands out. For Frame Job, the deferred issue #124 (Remove Background through Vision) is the on-device route.
Cinematic zoom optics: Glass Loupe and fisheye lenses, per-zoom 3D tilt and yaw, and Cap's 3D tracks with camera shots and focus blur. Screen Studio's on-device upscaler keeps zoomed text crisp.
Typing-aware automation: zooms aimed at the field being typed into, and typing stretches sped up automatically (Prequel, FocuSee, Screen Studio).
A voice-tracking teleprompter that follows your speech (Prequel), as opposed to a plain scrolling prompter.

An agent that EDITS the timeline (cuts, zooms, layouts, b-roll) with live preview and undo. Tella Agent (cloud, credits) and ScreenKite (local, 83 tools, plan-then-confirm) do this; Cap's and Loom's agents only manage recordings. Frame Job's local MCP plus Assistant over a full NLE, at no AI fee, is ahead here and should be marketed as such.

Describe-to-video and generated narration (Arcade, Clueso, Trupeer): script rewrite from rough narration, synced AI voiceover, multiple narrators, translation and dubbing. This is what product-demo creators pay for. Frame Job's bring-your-own-key model could offer it without a backend (for example a TTS key the user supplies).
Direct publishing and scheduling to YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, LinkedIn, X and Instagram, with social safe-zone overlays (Tella, and Screen Studio's Reel mode).
iPhone and iPad recording over USB straight into a device frame (Screen Studio). Rotato's freely directed 3D device shots up to 8K for launch videos.

Eye-contact correction (Tella, 2026-10-09) and camera LUTs and looks (Screen Studio, Tella, Prequel). Frame Job's grading and LUT engine already exceeds all of them and could be applied to the camera track with presets.

Pricing model as a differentiator: free and open source (OpenScreen's roughly 40k stars show the demand), or lifetime licences, against Screen Studio's subscription. Frame Job is free, open source, has no account, and keeps processing on-device.
Bring-your-own storage for share links (Cap: custom S3 or Google Drive, self-host with every feature). This fits Frame Job's no-backend, bring-your-own-key stance better than a hosted service would.

Frame Job's own edge over the whole segment: these recorders are shallow editors (Screen Studio and Prequel have no multi-track compositing, grading, HDR or pro audio, and export only MP4). Frame Job is a full NLE. The gap to close is the recorder-side event capture and the automatic polish layer built on top of it: cursor and keystroke data, auto zoom, cursor post-processing, camera layouts and cutout, and an auto-styled background frame. With that, its actions, motion, grading and agent stack would beat the polished-screencast tools at their own game.

toolu_014uVYBJdrky4QwWegETjYtv.segment: Screen-recording and tutorial / product-demo video tools, as of 2026-11-01: Screen Studio-style "polished screencast" recorders (Screen Studio, Cap, FocuSee, Prequel, ScreenKite, OpenScreen), all-in-one record-edit-host tools (Tella, Loom), long-standing screencast NLEs (Camtasia, ScreenFlow), device-mockup tools (Rotato, Screenhance), and AI product-video makers (Arcade, Clueso, Trupeer, Supademo). Method: vendor changelogs, help pages and official blogs first. Competitor blogs (Prequel, ScreenKite, Tella) and review aggregators are used only for corroboration and user sentiment, and are marked where used. I did not run any product. FRAME JOB'S BASELINE, from /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/docs/guide/screen-recording.md: the pointer and click rings are burned into the recorded picture, and no cursor, click or keystroke events are stored. The camera beside the screen is fixed in the bottom-right corner with no shape or layout control. The guide says "There's no keystroke or callout overlay". There is no camera background removal (issue #124, E9 Remove Background through Vision, is deferred). There are no share links. Zoom to Region (Z) is manual. On the other side, Frame Job already has a real multi-track NLE, grading and LUTs, HDR, a pro audio chain, filler and silence removal, motion graphics including keycaps and window frames, AV1/VP9 export, and the whole editor over local MCP plus an in-app Assistant.

tools.name: Screen Studio
tools.positioning: The tool that defined the category: a Mac-only recorder with a light editor that makes a raw screen recording look 'produced' with no editing skill (auto zoom, smooth cursor, backgrounds). Made by a bootstrapped team of five. Subscription-only since October 2025.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Praise: a polished result in minutes with near-zero editing, and auto zoom that 'just works' from clicks. Reviewers call the app quality 'unquestionable'. Complaints: subscription-only pricing ($29/mo or $108/yr; the $229 lifetime licence was withdrawn 2025-10-01 and users called the change 'misleading'). It is Mac-only, share links stop at 30 minutes, there is no team plan, and export is capped at 4K60. 4.0 shipped with regressions: export failures and stalls, a black editor on Intel/AMD Macs, and audio-enhancement features temporarily rolled back to beta on 2026-10-09. Those reports come from a competitor's blog (ScreenKite) quoting the vendor's Telegram group and X, so they are unverified.

headline_features.detail: Zooms toward the clicks captured during recording. The help page says clicks are the only trigger. Manual zooms are also auto-animated. 'Smart framing' places zooms so the webcam never covers the cursor, and vertical exports re-aim every zoom.
'Focuses on the areas where clicks occurred during your recording'. Each zoom can be Auto or Manual. A zoom placed where no click happened has nothing to aim at.

Smooth cursor (turns shaky paths into a glide), size, hide, hide when idle, loop cursor to its start for seamless loops, macOS or Touch style, rotate while moving, remove cursor shakes, stop movement at the end, sharp system cursors, click effects (circle or ripple), and click sounds.
'Optics-based' blur on fast cursor and zoom movement.
macOS wallpapers, gradients, your own image or Unsplash photos, with adjustable shadow angle, distance and softness, plus padding and inset. Presets can be saved and shared with a team.

Layouts: Fullscreen camera, Split screen, Camera overlay, Screen only and Camera cutout, with animated transitions between them. Camera cutout removes the background on-device with no green screen (beta). Also face tracking, 'Hide during silence', 12 camera looks, LUT import, crop and sharpen.

headline_features.feature: Glass Loupe and an on-device upscaler
headline_features.detail: A lens magnifies one area while the rest of the screen stays visible. A local AI model ('6.5× upscale') sharpens zoomed-in text.

headline_features.feature: Edit by transcript, plus filler words and pauses
headline_features.detail: Deleting a transcript sentence cuts the video. One pass shortens filler words and long pauses. On-device transcription, with cloud transcription optional. The edited transcript exports as SRT.
On-device transcription with styled, animated captions (font, colour, position, timing, animation).

headline_features.feature: Keystroke overlay ('Show shortcuts') and speeding up typing
headline_features.detail: Shows the keys pressed on screen. Typing detection (since 3.0) suggests speeding up typing stretches.
16:9, 1:1 and 9:16 with zooms, layouts and captions re-adjusted automatically. Reel mode overlays the Instagram or TikTok interface so you can check nothing is hidden behind it.

headline_features.feature: iPhone and iPad recording with device frames
headline_features.detail: Records over USB with a matching device mockup and nothing installed on the device. 3.5.2 (January 2026) added an iPhone 17 Pro Max frame.
Covers API keys or emails after recording. Highlight dims the rest of the frame. Automatic detection of such data after 4.0 is reported by a third party but not confirmed on a primary page.
On-device voice modes (Standard, Noise reduction, Podcast (beta)), background music, and AI voiceover from typed text, which sends the text to the cloud.

Links at 1080p60 for videos up to 30 minutes, with comments, private links and view counts. Editable projects up to 20 GB can be shared by link (beta in 4.0). Copy the finished video to the clipboard.

Resize the recorded window to an exact size, hide desktop icons, speaker notes, countdown, pause and resume, one global shortcut, and crash recovery that saves every 2 s. Built on ScreenCaptureKit. Export uses the media-engine hardware encoder (MP4 at 720p, 1080p or 4K up to 60 fps, or GIF).

tools.name: Camtasia (TechSmith: Camtasia Editor + Rev + Audiate + Camtasia Online)
tools.positioning: A veteran Windows and Mac screencast NLE for training and L&D teams. Renamed 'Camtasia Editor' on 2026-02-04 inside a 'Camtasia suite': Rev is a quick-layout recorder workflow, Audiate does text-based audio editing and AI voices, and Camtasia Online handles browser collaboration.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Praise: a deep timeline with callouts, annotations, quizzes and assets, the most manual control in the segment, a mature cursor toolkit, and fit for training teams. Complaints: a steep learning curve (42 G2 reviews mention it), subscription-only since the 2025 version, a high price for individuals (Essentials from $179.88/yr), resource-heavy with crashes on complex projects, audio-sync problems, licence server checks, and no built-in hosting (every share is an export plus an upload). G2 rates it 4.6/5 from 1,756 reviews.

headline_features.detail: Automatic zoom and pan for Rev media, made a screen effect in 2026.0.0. It analyses the recording to follow the cursor or the active window.

headline_features.feature: Rev quick layouts, looks and vertical
headline_features.detail: Rev picks size, layout, background, effects and filters in one step. Rev media can be adjusted on the canvas (2026.0.0). Vertical-aspect Looks and Layouts arrived in 2026.1.0.

Cursor smoothing (Camtasia recordings only), cursor path editing, the Cursor Path Creator for footage recorded elsewhere, scaling, replacing the pointer with a logo, glow, magnify, click effects, motion blur, and cursor elevation 'Always on Top' (its default became a setting in 2026.2.4).
Sends media to Camtasia Audiate (a separate product) for text-based editing, filler and hesitation removal, and audio clean-up.

AI voices, AI avatars, AI translation of audio and transcripts (7 languages, 9 dialects), AI script writing, AI image creator, AI titles, descriptions and chapters (in Screencast), and generative AI video. The features page is undated.
Social-style captions, applied directly to Rev media since 2026.0.0. Basic VTT import and export in 2026.1.0.
Removes the webcam background without a green screen and replaces it with an image or a dynamic background.

headline_features.feature: Snagit steps to a training video
headline_features.detail: Step-by-step screenshots from Snagit 2026.3+ become a ready-to-share training video automatically (2026.2.0).

headline_features.feature: Sync by audio, Zoom import, WebM export and SVG
headline_features.detail: Sync media timing by audio and import Zoom cloud recordings (2026.1.0). WebM export and Lottie-backed animated assets (2026.2.0). SVG Tiny 1.2 (2026.2.2).
A browser recorder and collaboration workflow, launched from the Home window from 2026.0.4. Third-party reviews say real-time multi-editor collaboration is still missing.

tools.name: ScreenFlow (Telestream)
tools.positioning: A long-standing Mac screencast editor with a perpetual-licence feel. It has been effectively in maintenance mode since its 2025 recording update.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Picked for a traditional record-and-edit timeline on the Mac with no account. The signal against it: no auto zoom, no AI captions and no transcript editing in any 2024–2026 release. The last feature release was 10.5 (2025-08-04), and 10.5.2 (2026-02-12) was fixes only. It is falling behind the Screen Studio-style tools.

headline_features.detail: Exclude ScreenFlow or specific apps, record a region, looped and timed recordings, native system audio with per-app audio and no driver, and a Recording Monitor preview with levels.

headline_features.feature: Background removal filter and cursor smoothing
headline_features.detail: An ML background-removal filter and cursor smoothing, both from 10.0 (2021). Nothing newer in this area.
10.5.2, with fixes for macOS 26.2 crashes and chroma-key export. No auto zoom or AI features are listed.

tools.name: Tella
tools.positioning: A cloud record-edit-host-publish platform for demos, tutorials, courses and async video (Mac, Windows, web, Chrome). By late 2026 it is the most agent-forward tool in the segment: a public API and MCP, Claude Code skills, an in-editor Tella Agent, and Tella Motion.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Praise: one place to record, edit (transcript, layouts, zooms), host with analytics, and publish straight to YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, LinkedIn and X. It ships weekly. Complaints and limits: no free plan (7-day trial, Pro from $13/user/mo), agent messages cost credits, Auto Capture cannot record localhost or desktop apps, and it is not built for frame-level or VFX editing (its own blog says so). Everything is cloud-hosted.

headline_features.feature: Auto zoom from clicks and cursor
headline_features.detail: Auto Zoom has existed since 2024-09-24 (Mac app). Auto Zooms V2 came 2025-09-24. Adaptive zooms became the default 2026-08-21, zooms auto-apply after recording since 2026-09-04, punch-in zooms arrived 2026-10-09, and presets (Subtle, Moderate, Focused, Intense) on 2026-10-23.

headline_features.feature: Effect panel: cursor, motion blur, highlights, blurs
headline_features.detail: One panel for zooms, animated cursors, blurs and highlights, with motion blur and cursor styling (2026-09-10). Animated cursor controls arrived 2026-08-28.

Multi-layouts and transitions since 2023–24, Auto Layouts (2025-07-10), Custom Layouts (2025-11-20), Vertical 50/50, Perspective layout, and Cut out camera background removal (2026-09-18). Also pop-out camera frames, the Blob camera style, animated borders, colour filters and LUTs (2026-09-25), and eye-contact correction (2026-10-09).
Text-based editing since 2024-05-02. Auto Cut (2025-07-22) finds mistakes, repeated lines and interruptions and removes them in one click. Silence detection combines amplitude with VAD (2026-05-22).

The API and MCP launched 2025-12-18. Clip API with cuts, zooms, blurs and layouts as MCP tools (2026-05-08). Batched apply_video_edits (2026-08-21). Storyboards (2026-09-04). Listed in Claude's Connector Directory (2026-08-06). An MCP settings page covers ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor and Codex (2026-07-24).
Open-source video workflows built for Claude Code, including local file editing and YouTube publishing.

Edits from a text description: cuts, zooms and layouts appear live and can be undone. It asks clarifying questions, makes 9:16 clips, and fills gaps with generated b-roll, sound effects or Motion graphics. Can use your own ChatGPT or Claude plan. It 'does not invent what you said or add narration'. Paid credits (4,500 a month per Pro seat).
An agent builds animated titles, charts, diagrams, lower thirds and b-roll on a keyframe and easing engine. There is no keyframe timeline for the user.
An AI records a walkthrough of a web page on Tella's servers at 4K60, started by Tella Agent or any MCP agent. It cannot record localhost, desktop or mobile apps.

Publish directly to YouTube, Shorts, LinkedIn, X and TikTok, with subtitle translations (2026-09-30). Instagram and Facebook added 2026-10-30. Scheduled publishing came 2026-10-16. Social safe zones for portrait (2026-05-22).
Hosted pages with analytics, comments, password protection, custom domains and embeds. Real-time co-editing in the new editor (2026-09-18).

tools.name: Loom (Atlassian)
tools.positioning: Async work video for teams, and in 2026 increasingly 'record for agents'. It is not a polish or screencast-effects tool.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Praise: the fastest record-and-share link, strong hosting, and a G2 rating of 4.7/5 from 2,349 reviews. Complaints: Trustpilot 1.4/5 from 204 reviews, login trouble after the Atlassian migration, seat-band price jumps, Business going from $18 to $20 (2026-06-05, per a third-party tracker), AI locked to Business + AI (about $24/user/mo), a 5-minute cap on the free plan, and no auto zoom.

headline_features.detail: A native rebuild for macOS 15+ that is about 80% smaller. Camera bubbles in circle, squircle, portrait or landscape that snap to the edges. Filters and custom backgrounds, a teleprompter below the camera, and automatic decluttering that hides desktop icons, the menu bar, tabs and notifications.

headline_features.feature: Record for agent and video prompts
headline_features.detail: Turns a narrated screen recording (transcript, click screenshots, links) into a step-by-step action plan or prompt for agents (Rovo, Claude, coding assistants), or into a Jira item. Magic Pen and a Selection tool mark UI elements. Business + AI and Enterprise plans only.
Agents (Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Codex) can pull transcripts, metadata and action items, add timestamped comments, and share or organise recordings. They cannot edit the video.

headline_features.feature: Edit by transcript, plus filler-word and silence removal
headline_features.detail: Trim by selecting words in the transcript. Toggles for Remove filler words and Remove Silence. Business + AI plan.
Loom AI generates titles, summaries and chapters, and runs workflows.

tools.name: Cap (cap.so)
tools.positioning: An open-source Loom and Screen Studio alternative for Mac and Windows: Studio Mode for polished local edits and Instant Mode for share links. Core code is AGPLv3 (the cap-camera* and scap-* crates are MIT). About 24.2k GitHub stars. Ships several times a week. Moved to a native GPUI app in 0.6.1.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Praise: free for personal use, a $58 lifetime desktop licence, open source and self-hostable, custom S3 or Google Drive storage, near-identical Mac and Windows apps, and very fast iteration. Complaints: a younger product with a smaller editing set (per Tella's comparison), free share links capped at 5 minutes, self-hosting falls on you, and some confusion about pricing. Licence note for Frame Job (Apache-2.0): Cap's AGPL code cannot be carried over, the same rule as Concat.

headline_features.detail: Experimental from 0.3.62 (2025-08-06). Spring-based zoom with cursor and display motion blur in 0.5.4 (2026-07-06). Keeps a resting cursor in view, ignores cursor movement in cut sections, and works on multi-take timelines (0.6.1 and 0.6.2).

Custom cursor capture on by default (0.3.67). High-resolution SVG cursors. Hide an inactive cursor with a fade (0.3.74). Smooth and Fast cursor presets, and a cursor-only ProRes 4444 export (0.4.82). Cursor styles with click ripples (0.6.0). Smoothed cursors settle where the mouse stopped (0.6.2).
3D tracks give automatic or custom camera shots with perspective, easing and focus blur. Style tracks change the background, camera or cursor for one section only.
Blur or remove the camera background on macOS, in preview and export (0.6.0). Better removal that keeps only the main person (0.6.1).

headline_features.feature: Keyboard press overlay track and caption tracks
headline_features.detail: A keyboard-press overlay track and caption tracks in the timeline (0.4.81). Local Whisper and Parakeet transcription. Caption presets and animations with SRT and VTT export (0.5.3).
A word-level transcript editor (0.4.82, 0.5.3).

headline_features.feature: Cap for agents: CLI, skill and local MCP server
headline_features.detail: Agents (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor) can record, export, upload and share, and read transcripts, AI summaries, chapters, comments and analytics, with JSON output and confirmation before changes. The notes do NOT say agents can edit the timeline (zooms or cuts).
Built-in teleprompter, clip transitions, and blur and pixelate masks (0.5.7). Scenes with split screen (0.5.1). Decorative frames (0.5.4). Animated gradient backgrounds and Studio Sound (0.6.0).
9:16 area and window presets, and portrait videos fill vertical projects (0.6.2). Image backgrounds are re-cropped when the aspect ratio changes (0.6.1).

Free for personal use (4K60 export, 5-minute links). Desktop $29/yr or $58 lifetime (commercial use, 20 links a month). Pro $12/user/mo ($8.16 billed annually) with unlimited links, AI titles, summaries and chapters, custom domain, password-protected shares, viewer analytics, and custom S3 or Google Drive storage. Self-hosting keeps all features.

tools.name: FocuSee (iMobie)
tools.positioning: A Windows and Mac Screen Studio-style recorder with auto zoom, cursor effects, an AI avatar and a beauty filter. Sold as an annual licence or a lifetime licence.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Picked as the Windows option for Screen Studio-style output, with a lifetime licence ($199.99, or from $49.99/yr per Tella's comparison). Weaknesses: hosting is a paid add-on, there is no team workspace, and advanced AI features need credits.

headline_features.feature: Auto zoom from clicks and typing
headline_features.detail: Auto typing recognition generates zooms from typing (2.4.0 Mac, 2026-07-16; improved in 2.4.1). Smart speed-up of typing sections.
Custom cursor angle, dynamic direction, idle duration, path smoothness, and end position (2.5.0).

headline_features.feature: 3D motion, spotlight, motion blur and keyboard shortcut capture
headline_features.detail: Tilt and perspective that follow the cursor, cursor highlighting, spotlight, motion blur, and keyboard shortcut capture.
PiP and full-screen layouts that switch mid-video, AI background blur or replacement in post, a beauty filter, and custom layout presets (2.5.0).

headline_features.feature: AI subtitles, AI avatar, teleprompter and audio clean-up
headline_features.detail: Subtitles in 50+ languages with SRT import. An AI virtual avatar so you can appear without your face. Teleprompter. Voice enhancement, noise reduction, and filler and silence removal.

headline_features.feature: Resizing for social platforms and share links
headline_features.detail: One-click aspect-ratio resizing for TikTok, YouTube, Instagram and others. Full-screen support for vertical video (2.3.5 Windows). Share links with password and permissions.

tools.name: Prequel (prequel.sh) — new entrant
tools.positioning: A 'cinematic' Mac screen recorder that 'does the editing for you', aimed straight at Screen Studio 4. Launched on Product Hunt 2026-08-30 (198 upvotes, #4 of the day). Ships almost daily. Apple Silicon and macOS 14+ only. All processing is local.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Pitched on price ($39 lifetime or $9/mo, the same app on both) and on matching Screen Studio 4 features within weeks of it. Thin independent feedback so far: one Product Hunt review at 4/5, and a commenter who wanted a lifetime option, which was added at launch. Its own comparison posts are marketing.

headline_features.feature: Auto zoom from clicks and typing, with 3D tilt and yaw
headline_features.detail: Zooms target the cursor, a drawn region, or the field being typed into (typing needs the Accessibility permission). Level, speed, tilt, yaw and blur falloff are set per zoom. Each zoom is an ordinary timeline slice.
A Loupe zoom method (v0.0.35, 2026-10-02) with light spill (v0.1.1). Fisheye zoom (v0.7.0, 2026-10-21).

The pointer is stored as data, not burned into the picture (v0.0.26). Fifteen pointer styles, resized to stay visible during zooms, smoothed while moving, hidden after stillness, and motion-blurred. Click effects (ripples, confetti, chalk), plus click and typing sounds.

Fourteen layouts, switchable per clip. Camera shapes (circle, squircle, rounded, wide, portrait, 'Follow me'). Camera background removal (v0.0.19) and a cut-out layout (v0.8.1). Camera colour looks. Rotation at any angle.

headline_features.feature: Teleprompter in the notch with voice tracking
headline_features.detail: The script sits under the camera notch and highlights each word as it is spoken. It pauses when you go off script and catches up when you skip ahead.

headline_features.feature: Subtitles and edit by deleting sentences
headline_features.detail: On-device transcription. Fix a word by typing over it, or delete a sentence to cut it. Styles: Blur in, Subtitle, Highlight and Band.

headline_features.feature: CLI and a Claude Code skill
headline_features.detail: A `prequel` command-line tool and a Claude Code skill (v0.1.0).

MP4 (H.264 or HEVC) up to 4K and 120 fps, constant frame rate, VideoToolbox plus Metal. Framing is stored as proportions so a layout survives a switch to 9:16. Presets for YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, Reels, X and LinkedIn. Filters (Dream, Dither, Lost signal). Share links involve an upload.
$39 lifetime (5 GB of shared recordings kept 3 months) or $9/mo (unlimited sharing). A 7-day trial with no watermark.

tools.name: ScreenKite — new entrant
tools.positioning: A free native Mac recorder and editor (exports watermarked until Pro) whose pitch is that a local AI agent edits the recording with the same tools the UI uses. Pro is $79.99 one-time for 3 Macs, rising to $99.99 after 2026-10-31. It also publishes aggressive blog posts against Screen Studio.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Picked by creators who already pay for Claude Code or Codex and want agent editing with no extra AI fee, plus a one-time price. Every source is the vendor's own marketing (version 1.18, September 2026), so treat it as unverified. This is the closest competitor to Frame Job's MCP and Assistant model.

headline_features.detail: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Grok Build and Kimi drive the same editing tools as the UI. Meaning-changing edits return a plan with confirm:false and apply with confirm:true. Edits undo like clicks. There is a CLI (`screenkite agent export --json`). MCP is not stated.

headline_features.feature: Auto zoom, transcript cutting and on-device captions
headline_features.detail: Auto zoom on clicks and keystrokes, transcript-based cutting, and on-device captions with WhisperKit (Apple Silicon; Intel falls back to ElevenLabs cloud). Backgrounds, padding, rounded corners and shadows. Export up to 1080p60 H.264.

tools.name: OpenScreen (open source)
tools.positioning: 'Your free, open-source alternative to Screen Studio' (MIT). About 40k GitHub stars, which is the strongest adoption signal for a free Screen Studio-style tool. Archived after v1.5.0 (2026-06-06), with a community continuation at getopenscreen/openscreen.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Free with no paid tiers, and free for commercial use. The author warns it is 'not production grade and you'll hit bugs'. Its star count shows how much demand there is for a non-subscription, open polished-screencast tool.

headline_features.detail: Window or screen recording with mic and system audio. Webcam PiP with shapes. Auto or manual zooms that follow the cursor. Cursor size, smoothing, click effects and post-recording path smoothing. On-device captions. Wallpaper and gradient backgrounds. Motion blur. Crop, trim and speed. Annotations. MP4 or GIF in several aspect ratios.

tools.name: Rotato (and Screenhance) — device mockups
tools.positioning: 3D device-mockup renderers for app launch videos and store assets, alongside screen recorders rather than replacing them.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Rotato gives freely directed 3D (camera, lighting, depth of field) on 30+ hand-built devices, a one-time Mac licence, and offline rendering. The criticism: animation is template-driven rather than keyframed (Screenhance's comparison), and the licence does not cover every future update. Screenhance offers preset 3D device templates plus screen-recording 'Studio' and store-set automation, with less freedom than Rotato.

headline_features.detail: Phones, tablets, laptops and desktops. Timeline-based camera and device animation, reflections, shadows, depth of field, clay styles. Renders up to 8K. Exports H.264 and HEVC, transparent HEVC with alpha or ProRes 4444, image sequences, and Lottie. iPhone mirroring and USB screen recording. A Figma plugin.
Device turns, laptop lid openings, floating arcs and an iPhone Duo fold, plus App Store screenshot sets.

tools.name: Arcade (arcade.software) — AI product video
tools.positioning: Began as interactive product demos and is now an AI product-video generator: you describe the video, and an agent writes the script, builds scenes, records the product and adds voiceover.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Picked for marketing and product teams who want a narrated launch or feature video without recording or narrating themselves. AI-video Pro is about $59/mo per a third-party list. A vendor benchmark claims AI voiceover lifts completion 14% (unverified).

headline_features.detail: Arcade asks questions, drafts a plan and generates after you approve (2026-05-27). Chat edits restructure scenes and change messaging (2026-06-25). The agent watches its own output and fixes visible problems (2026-09-17). Choice of model per video: Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 or Haiku 5.5, plus 3D prompts (2026-10-20).

Chrome extension recordings get a smooth cursor, highlighted clicks and automatic zooms (2026-10-20). Desktop cursor animations gained motion blur and click feedback (2026-06-10). Screen, camera and voice with switching in one take (2026-09-29).

ElevenLabs v3 with emotion control (2026-01-26). Up to three narrators (2026-09-29). Brand-kit pronunciations and editing the whole voiceover as one script (2026-08-19). An AI voice per language for translations.

tools.name: Clueso / Trupeer — AI product-video makers
tools.positioning: Turn a rough screen recording into a polished narrated product or training video: AI script rewrite, AI voiceover, auto zoom on clicks, avatars, translation, and a matching written guide.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: G2 reviewers describe going from a day of recording and editing to minutes. The criticism: AI voiceover can sound synthetic, and complex apps need manual zoom fixes. Clueso starts around $50/mo per a third-party list. Vendor pages are undated, so the 2026 state is not confirmed.

headline_features.feature: Script rewrite and synced AI voiceover (Clueso)
headline_features.detail: Transcribes your narration, polishes it into an editable script, and regenerates a synced AI voiceover. Auto zoom on clicks, removal of mistakes and dead air, callouts, branding, translation with AI voice, and a step-by-step text guide with screenshots.
Zooms added automatically on every click and action. AI voiceover in many accents (the vendor's figures conflict: 65+ and 120+). A stock or custom avatar narrator. Filler removal. Auto chapters.

tools.name: Supademo
tools.positioning: An interactive-demo builder with a growing video editor. Included only because it edits video.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Picked for clickable demos with AI voiceover. Video-side zoom is behind the others.

headline_features.feature: Video editor redesign and AI voiceover
headline_features.detail: A redesigned video editor (splitting, trimming, timeline) in February 2026. Voiceovers 2.0 with an expressive mode in June 2026. More voiceover languages in September 2026.

headline_features.feature: Video zoom and pan, and chapters
headline_features.detail: Described as 'coming next' in the September 2026 recap.

trends.trend: The cursor is captured as data, not burned into the picture, and everything Screen Studio made popular rests on that
trends.evidence: Auto zoom, cursor smoothing, resizing, hide-when-idle, restyling, click effects, looping and motion blur all require pointer position and click and key events recorded separately from the frames. Prequel made 'Pointer no longer baked into recordings' a changelog item (v0.0.26). Cap captures custom cursors by default and even exports a cursor-only ProRes 4444. Screen Studio's auto zoom 'focuses on the areas where clicks occurred during your recording'. Camtasia's cursor smoothing works only on Camtasia's own recordings for the same reason. Frame Job's recorder burns the pointer and click rings into the movie and stores no events, so none of this category's table stakes can be built until that changes.

trends.trend: Auto zoom has moved from 'zoom on clicks' to cinematic camera work: typing triggers, spring physics, motion blur, loupe and fisheye lenses, 3D perspective, and zooms that re-aim for vertical
trends.evidence: FocuSee added typing-triggered zooms (2026-07-16). Prequel aims at the field being typed into and has per-zoom tilt and yaw (2026). Cap has spring-based zoom with motion blur (2026-07-06) and 3D tracks with camera shots and focus blur (2026-08-31). Screen Studio added Glass Loupe (2026-10-02). Prequel added Loupe (2026-10-02) and fisheye (2026-10-21). Tella added punch-in zooms and intensity presets (October 2026). Screen Studio uses an on-device upscaler so zoomed text stays sharp.

trends.trend: The presenter camera gets pro treatment: cutout without a green screen, face tracking, hide-during-silence, looks and LUTs, eye contact, shapes and split layouts
trends.evidence: Screen Studio 4 (2026-10-02): camera cutout (beta), face tracking, 'Hide during silence', 12 looks plus LUTs, split screen. Cap 0.6.0 and 0.6.1: background blur and removal. Tella: Cut out (2026-09-18), LUTs (2026-09-25), eye-contact correction (2026-10-09). Prequel: cutout (2026-09-13). FocuSee: beauty filter. Loom for Mac: bubble shapes and backgrounds (2026-10-07).

trends.trend: Every recorder now ships an agent surface, but most agents only drive record, export and share, not the edit
trends.evidence: Tella: API and MCP (2025-12-18), clip-editing MCP tools (2026-05-08), Claude Code skills (2026-07-12), in-editor Tella Agent (public beta 2026-10-16/30). Cap: CLI, skill and local MCP (2026-07-20), with recording, export, sharing and transcripts but no timeline editing listed. Prequel: CLI plus a Claude Code skill (2026-10-05). ScreenKite: 83 agent editing tools with plan-then-confirm (vendor claim). Loom: Record for agent plus Atlassian MCP (2026-10-22). Arcade: a describe-to-video agent on Claude models (2026-10-20). Frame Job's whole-editor local MCP plus an in-app Assistant, with every edit an undo step, is no longer unique in kind. It is still the deepest in scope, being a full NLE.

trends.trend: Edit by transcript plus one-pass filler, pause and mistake removal has become standard in recorders, not just in Descript
trends.evidence: Screen Studio 4 (transcript editing, filler words and pauses). Cap word-level transcript editor (2026-04-02). Tella Auto Cut, which removes mistakes and repeated lines (2025-07-22). Loom (Business + AI). Prequel (delete a sentence). Camtasia via Audiate's Edit as Text.

trends.trend: Generated narration and describe-to-video in product-demo tools
trends.evidence: Arcade writes the script, builds scenes and voices them, with chat editing and an agent that checks its own output. Clueso rewrites your narration into a clean script and regenerates a synced AI voiceover. Trupeer and Camtasia/Audiate offer AI voices, avatars and translation. Screen Studio has cloud AI voiceover from typed text. Tella deliberately 'does not invent what you said or add narration'.

trends.trend: One recording, every aspect ratio, with zooms and layouts re-framed automatically, social safe zones, and direct publishing
trends.evidence: Screen Studio re-aims zooms for 9:16 and has Reel mode safe-zone overlays. Prequel stores framing as proportions. Cap added 9:16 presets and portrait fill (2026-10-28). Camtasia Rev added vertical looks (2026-04-14). Tella added social safe zones (2026-05-22) and direct publishing to YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, LinkedIn, X, Instagram and Facebook (2026-09-30 and 10-30).

trends.trend: A teleprompter built into the recorder
trends.evidence: Prequel's notch teleprompter with voice tracking (2026-09-18). Cap teleprompter (2026-07-20). Loom for Mac teleprompter (2026-10-07). FocuSee teleprompter. Screen Studio speaker notes.

trends.trend: Backlash against subscription pricing, and a wave of lifetime, free and open-source alternatives
trends.evidence: Screen Studio dropped its lifetime licence on 2025-10-01 and users called the move 'misleading'. It now charges $29/mo or $108/yr. Camtasia has been subscription-only since 2025. Alternatives: OpenScreen (MIT, about 40k stars), Cap (open source, $58 lifetime), Prequel ($39 lifetime), ScreenKite ($79.99 one-time), FocuSee ($199.99 lifetime). Frame Job is free, open source and bring-your-own-key, which is a strong position in this fight.

trends.trend: Hosted share links are how the category makes money, and bring-your-own storage is emerging
trends.evidence: Screen Studio links (30-minute cap, comments, view counts). Cap Pro links with a custom domain, analytics and custom S3 or Google Drive storage, plus full-featured self-hosting. Tella's hosted pages and analytics. Prequel links tied to plan storage. Camtasia and ScreenFlow have no hosting, which reviewers flag.

trends.trend: On-device processing and native performance as selling points, and stability as the risk
trends.evidence: Screen Studio says recording, transcripts, voice enhancement, face tracking and export are all local, with 3x faster exports in 4.0. Prequel, ScreenKite (WhisperKit) and Loom rebuilt native for Mac (2026-10-07). Cap moved from Tauri to native GPUI (0.6.1, 2026-10-20). Screen Studio 4.0's reported export failures and feature rollbacks show that reliability on long projects is still a weak point.

trends.trend: Masking sensitive on-screen data
trends.evidence: Screen Studio's sensitive-data masks for API keys and emails, plus Highlight. Cap's blur and pixelate masks (2026-07-20). Tella's blurs and highlights that work during zooms. Loom for Mac's automatic decluttering of tabs, bookmarks and notifications.

table_stakes: Recording a display, a window or a dragged area, with camera, mic and system audio as SEPARATE tracks; pause and resume, countdown, a global shortcut, and crash recovery. Frame Job has most of this, but no area capture.

Cursor and click (and increasingly keystroke) events captured alongside the video, so the pointer can be resized, restyled, smoothed, hidden when idle or removed after recording, with click highlights and click sounds. Frame Job: missing, because the pointer is burned in.

Automatic zoom from clicks (and now typing) that produces editable zoom segments on the timeline, plus manual zoom, eased or spring motion, and motion blur on zoom and pan. Frame Job has manual Zoom to Region actions only.
Background canvas around the recording: wallpapers, gradients, images, padding, rounded corners, shadow and inset. Saved and shareable style presets.

Camera overlay with shapes (circle, squircle, rounded) and layouts (PiP corner, side by side, stacked, full camera, screen only) that switch mid-video with animated transitions, placed so it never covers the cursor. Frame Job: fixed bottom-right corner.
On-device auto-captions with styled and animated presets and SRT/VTT export. Frame Job has this.
Edit by transcript plus one-click removal of filler words and silences. Frame Job has filler and silence removal; check that deleting text in a transcript view cuts the video.
Speeding up selected sections (especially typing) and trim, cut and crop.
Keystroke and shortcut overlay generated from recorded key events. Frame Job has only a manual keycap graphic.
Switching the output to 16:9, 9:16 or 1:1 with zooms, layouts and captions re-framed automatically.
Blur or pixelate masks and highlight or spotlight for sensitive or important regions. Frame Job has obscure and spotlight.
Voice clean-up (noise reduction or 'studio sound') and background music. Frame Job's audio chain is ahead of the whole segment here.
Export up to 4K60 MP4 and GIF using the hardware encoder.
Some way to share: a hosted link with comments and views, or at least copy to clipboard or direct publish. Frame Job has none.
differentiators: Camera cutout without a green screen, plus face tracking and hide-the-camera-during-silence (Screen Studio 4, Cap 0.6, Tella, Prequel). Shipped by the leaders in September–October 2026 but still beta at Screen Studio, so a well-made version still stands out. For Frame Job, the deferred issue #124 (Remove Background through Vision) is the on-device route.
Cinematic zoom optics: Glass Loupe and fisheye lenses, per-zoom 3D tilt and yaw, and Cap's 3D tracks with camera shots and focus blur. Screen Studio's on-device upscaler keeps zoomed text crisp.
Typing-aware automation: zooms aimed at the field being typed into, and typing stretches sped up automatically (Prequel, FocuSee, Screen Studio).
A voice-tracking teleprompter that follows your speech (Prequel), as opposed to a plain scrolling prompter.

An agent that EDITS the timeline (cuts, zooms, layouts, b-roll) with live preview and undo. Tella Agent (cloud, credits) and ScreenKite (local, 83 tools, plan-then-confirm) do this; Cap's and Loom's agents only manage recordings. Frame Job's local MCP plus Assistant over a full NLE, at no AI fee, is ahead here and should be marketed as such.

Describe-to-video and generated narration (Arcade, Clueso, Trupeer): script rewrite from rough narration, synced AI voiceover, multiple narrators, translation and dubbing. This is what product-demo creators pay for. Frame Job's bring-your-own-key model could offer it without a backend (for example a TTS key the user supplies).
Direct publishing and scheduling to YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, LinkedIn, X and Instagram, with social safe-zone overlays (Tella, and Screen Studio's Reel mode).
iPhone and iPad recording over USB straight into a device frame (Screen Studio). Rotato's freely directed 3D device shots up to 8K for launch videos.

Eye-contact correction (Tella, 2026-10-09) and camera LUTs and looks (Screen Studio, Tella, Prequel). Frame Job's grading and LUT engine already exceeds all of them and could be applied to the camera track with presets.

Pricing model as a differentiator: free and open source (OpenScreen's roughly 40k stars show the demand), or lifetime licences, against Screen Studio's subscription. Frame Job is free, open source, has no account, and keeps processing on-device.
Bring-your-own storage for share links (Cap: custom S3 or Google Drive, self-host with every feature). This fits Frame Job's no-backend, bring-your-own-key stance better than a hosted service would.

Frame Job's own edge over the whole segment: these recorders are shallow editors (Screen Studio and Prequel have no multi-track compositing, grading, HDR or pro audio, and export only MP4). Frame Job is a full NLE. The gap to close is the recorder-side event capture and the automatic polish layer built on top of it: cursor and keystroke data, auto zoom, cursor post-processing, camera layouts and cutout, and an auto-styled background frame. With that, its actions, motion, grading and agent stack would beat the polished-screencast tools at their own game.

data.segment: Screen-recording and tutorial / product-demo video tools, as of 2026-11-01: Screen Studio-style "polished screencast" recorders (Screen Studio, Cap, FocuSee, Prequel, ScreenKite, OpenScreen), all-in-one record-edit-host tools (Tella, Loom), long-standing screencast NLEs (Camtasia, ScreenFlow), device-mockup tools (Rotato, Screenhance), and AI product-video makers (Arcade, Clueso, Trupeer, Supademo). Method: vendor changelogs, help pages and official blogs first. Competitor blogs (Prequel, ScreenKite, Tella) and review aggregators are used only for corroboration and user sentiment, and are marked where used. I did not run any product. FRAME JOB'S BASELINE, from /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/docs/guide/screen-recording.md: the pointer and click rings are burned into the recorded picture, and no cursor, click or keystroke events are stored. The camera beside the screen is fixed in the bottom-right corner with no shape or layout control. The guide says "There's no keystroke or callout overlay". There is no camera background removal (issue #124, E9 Remove Background through Vision, is deferred). There are no share links. Zoom to Region (Z) is manual. On the other side, Frame Job already has a real multi-track NLE, grading and LUTs, HDR, a pro audio chain, filler and silence removal, motion graphics including keycaps and window frames, AV1/VP9 export, and the whole editor over local MCP plus an in-app Assistant.

tools.name: Screen Studio
tools.positioning: The tool that defined the category: a Mac-only recorder with a light editor that makes a raw screen recording look 'produced' with no editing skill (auto zoom, smooth cursor, backgrounds). Made by a bootstrapped team of five. Subscription-only since October 2025.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Praise: a polished result in minutes with near-zero editing, and auto zoom that 'just works' from clicks. Reviewers call the app quality 'unquestionable'. Complaints: subscription-only pricing ($29/mo or $108/yr; the $229 lifetime licence was withdrawn 2025-10-01 and users called the change 'misleading'). It is Mac-only, share links stop at 30 minutes, there is no team plan, and export is capped at 4K60. 4.0 shipped with regressions: export failures and stalls, a black editor on Intel/AMD Macs, and audio-enhancement features temporarily rolled back to beta on 2026-10-09. Those reports come from a competitor's blog (ScreenKite) quoting the vendor's Telegram group and X, so they are unverified.

headline_features.detail: Zooms toward the clicks captured during recording. The help page says clicks are the only trigger. Manual zooms are also auto-animated. 'Smart framing' places zooms so the webcam never covers the cursor, and vertical exports re-aim every zoom.
'Focuses on the areas where clicks occurred during your recording'. Each zoom can be Auto or Manual. A zoom placed where no click happened has nothing to aim at.

Smooth cursor (turns shaky paths into a glide), size, hide, hide when idle, loop cursor to its start for seamless loops, macOS or Touch style, rotate while moving, remove cursor shakes, stop movement at the end, sharp system cursors, click effects (circle or ripple), and click sounds.
'Optics-based' blur on fast cursor and zoom movement.
macOS wallpapers, gradients, your own image or Unsplash photos, with adjustable shadow angle, distance and softness, plus padding and inset. Presets can be saved and shared with a team.

Layouts: Fullscreen camera, Split screen, Camera overlay, Screen only and Camera cutout, with animated transitions between them. Camera cutout removes the background on-device with no green screen (beta). Also face tracking, 'Hide during silence', 12 camera looks, LUT import, crop and sharpen.

headline_features.feature: Glass Loupe and an on-device upscaler
headline_features.detail: A lens magnifies one area while the rest of the screen stays visible. A local AI model ('6.5× upscale') sharpens zoomed-in text.

headline_features.feature: Edit by transcript, plus filler words and pauses
headline_features.detail: Deleting a transcript sentence cuts the video. One pass shortens filler words and long pauses. On-device transcription, with cloud transcription optional. The edited transcript exports as SRT.
On-device transcription with styled, animated captions (font, colour, position, timing, animation).

headline_features.feature: Keystroke overlay ('Show shortcuts') and speeding up typing
headline_features.detail: Shows the keys pressed on screen. Typing detection (since 3.0) suggests speeding up typing stretches.
16:9, 1:1 and 9:16 with zooms, layouts and captions re-adjusted automatically. Reel mode overlays the Instagram or TikTok interface so you can check nothing is hidden behind it.

headline_features.feature: iPhone and iPad recording with device frames
headline_features.detail: Records over USB with a matching device mockup and nothing installed on the device. 3.5.2 (January 2026) added an iPhone 17 Pro Max frame.
Covers API keys or emails after recording. Highlight dims the rest of the frame. Automatic detection of such data after 4.0 is reported by a third party but not confirmed on a primary page.
On-device voice modes (Standard, Noise reduction, Podcast (beta)), background music, and AI voiceover from typed text, which sends the text to the cloud.

Links at 1080p60 for videos up to 30 minutes, with comments, private links and view counts. Editable projects up to 20 GB can be shared by link (beta in 4.0). Copy the finished video to the clipboard.

Resize the recorded window to an exact size, hide desktop icons, speaker notes, countdown, pause and resume, one global shortcut, and crash recovery that saves every 2 s. Built on ScreenCaptureKit. Export uses the media-engine hardware encoder (MP4 at 720p, 1080p or 4K up to 60 fps, or GIF).

tools.name: Camtasia (TechSmith: Camtasia Editor + Rev + Audiate + Camtasia Online)
tools.positioning: A veteran Windows and Mac screencast NLE for training and L&D teams. Renamed 'Camtasia Editor' on 2026-02-04 inside a 'Camtasia suite': Rev is a quick-layout recorder workflow, Audiate does text-based audio editing and AI voices, and Camtasia Online handles browser collaboration.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Praise: a deep timeline with callouts, annotations, quizzes and assets, the most manual control in the segment, a mature cursor toolkit, and fit for training teams. Complaints: a steep learning curve (42 G2 reviews mention it), subscription-only since the 2025 version, a high price for individuals (Essentials from $179.88/yr), resource-heavy with crashes on complex projects, audio-sync problems, licence server checks, and no built-in hosting (every share is an export plus an upload). G2 rates it 4.6/5 from 1,756 reviews.

headline_features.detail: Automatic zoom and pan for Rev media, made a screen effect in 2026.0.0. It analyses the recording to follow the cursor or the active window.

headline_features.feature: Rev quick layouts, looks and vertical
headline_features.detail: Rev picks size, layout, background, effects and filters in one step. Rev media can be adjusted on the canvas (2026.0.0). Vertical-aspect Looks and Layouts arrived in 2026.1.0.

Cursor smoothing (Camtasia recordings only), cursor path editing, the Cursor Path Creator for footage recorded elsewhere, scaling, replacing the pointer with a logo, glow, magnify, click effects, motion blur, and cursor elevation 'Always on Top' (its default became a setting in 2026.2.4).
Sends media to Camtasia Audiate (a separate product) for text-based editing, filler and hesitation removal, and audio clean-up.

AI voices, AI avatars, AI translation of audio and transcripts (7 languages, 9 dialects), AI script writing, AI image creator, AI titles, descriptions and chapters (in Screencast), and generative AI video. The features page is undated.
Social-style captions, applied directly to Rev media since 2026.0.0. Basic VTT import and export in 2026.1.0.
Removes the webcam background without a green screen and replaces it with an image or a dynamic background.

headline_features.feature: Snagit steps to a training video
headline_features.detail: Step-by-step screenshots from Snagit 2026.3+ become a ready-to-share training video automatically (2026.2.0).

headline_features.feature: Sync by audio, Zoom import, WebM export and SVG
headline_features.detail: Sync media timing by audio and import Zoom cloud recordings (2026.1.0). WebM export and Lottie-backed animated assets (2026.2.0). SVG Tiny 1.2 (2026.2.2).
A browser recorder and collaboration workflow, launched from the Home window from 2026.0.4. Third-party reviews say real-time multi-editor collaboration is still missing.

tools.name: ScreenFlow (Telestream)
tools.positioning: A long-standing Mac screencast editor with a perpetual-licence feel. It has been effectively in maintenance mode since its 2025 recording update.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Picked for a traditional record-and-edit timeline on the Mac with no account. The signal against it: no auto zoom, no AI captions and no transcript editing in any 2024–2026 release. The last feature release was 10.5 (2025-08-04), and 10.5.2 (2026-02-12) was fixes only. It is falling behind the Screen Studio-style tools.

headline_features.detail: Exclude ScreenFlow or specific apps, record a region, looped and timed recordings, native system audio with per-app audio and no driver, and a Recording Monitor preview with levels.

headline_features.feature: Background removal filter and cursor smoothing
headline_features.detail: An ML background-removal filter and cursor smoothing, both from 10.0 (2021). Nothing newer in this area.
10.5.2, with fixes for macOS 26.2 crashes and chroma-key export. No auto zoom or AI features are listed.

tools.name: Tella
tools.positioning: A cloud record-edit-host-publish platform for demos, tutorials, courses and async video (Mac, Windows, web, Chrome). By late 2026 it is the most agent-forward tool in the segment: a public API and MCP, Claude Code skills, an in-editor Tella Agent, and Tella Motion.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Praise: one place to record, edit (transcript, layouts, zooms), host with analytics, and publish straight to YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, LinkedIn and X. It ships weekly. Complaints and limits: no free plan (7-day trial, Pro from $13/user/mo), agent messages cost credits, Auto Capture cannot record localhost or desktop apps, and it is not built for frame-level or VFX editing (its own blog says so). Everything is cloud-hosted.

headline_features.feature: Auto zoom from clicks and cursor
headline_features.detail: Auto Zoom has existed since 2024-09-24 (Mac app). Auto Zooms V2 came 2025-09-24. Adaptive zooms became the default 2026-08-21, zooms auto-apply after recording since 2026-09-04, punch-in zooms arrived 2026-10-09, and presets (Subtle, Moderate, Focused, Intense) on 2026-10-23.

headline_features.feature: Effect panel: cursor, motion blur, highlights, blurs
headline_features.detail: One panel for zooms, animated cursors, blurs and highlights, with motion blur and cursor styling (2026-09-10). Animated cursor controls arrived 2026-08-28.

Multi-layouts and transitions since 2023–24, Auto Layouts (2025-07-10), Custom Layouts (2025-11-20), Vertical 50/50, Perspective layout, and Cut out camera background removal (2026-09-18). Also pop-out camera frames, the Blob camera style, animated borders, colour filters and LUTs (2026-09-25), and eye-contact correction (2026-10-09).
Text-based editing since 2024-05-02. Auto Cut (2025-07-22) finds mistakes, repeated lines and interruptions and removes them in one click. Silence detection combines amplitude with VAD (2026-05-22).

The API and MCP launched 2025-12-18. Clip API with cuts, zooms, blurs and layouts as MCP tools (2026-05-08). Batched apply_video_edits (2026-08-21). Storyboards (2026-09-04). Listed in Claude's Connector Directory (2026-08-06). An MCP settings page covers ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor and Codex (2026-07-24).
Open-source video workflows built for Claude Code, including local file editing and YouTube publishing.

Edits from a text description: cuts, zooms and layouts appear live and can be undone. It asks clarifying questions, makes 9:16 clips, and fills gaps with generated b-roll, sound effects or Motion graphics. Can use your own ChatGPT or Claude plan. It 'does not invent what you said or add narration'. Paid credits (4,500 a month per Pro seat).
An agent builds animated titles, charts, diagrams, lower thirds and b-roll on a keyframe and easing engine. There is no keyframe timeline for the user.
An AI records a walkthrough of a web page on Tella's servers at 4K60, started by Tella Agent or any MCP agent. It cannot record localhost, desktop or mobile apps.

Publish directly to YouTube, Shorts, LinkedIn, X and TikTok, with subtitle translations (2026-09-30). Instagram and Facebook added 2026-10-30. Scheduled publishing came 2026-10-16. Social safe zones for portrait (2026-05-22).
Hosted pages with analytics, comments, password protection, custom domains and embeds. Real-time co-editing in the new editor (2026-09-18).

tools.name: Loom (Atlassian)
tools.positioning: Async work video for teams, and in 2026 increasingly 'record for agents'. It is not a polish or screencast-effects tool.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Praise: the fastest record-and-share link, strong hosting, and a G2 rating of 4.7/5 from 2,349 reviews. Complaints: Trustpilot 1.4/5 from 204 reviews, login trouble after the Atlassian migration, seat-band price jumps, Business going from $18 to $20 (2026-06-05, per a third-party tracker), AI locked to Business + AI (about $24/user/mo), a 5-minute cap on the free plan, and no auto zoom.

headline_features.detail: A native rebuild for macOS 15+ that is about 80% smaller. Camera bubbles in circle, squircle, portrait or landscape that snap to the edges. Filters and custom backgrounds, a teleprompter below the camera, and automatic decluttering that hides desktop icons, the menu bar, tabs and notifications.

headline_features.feature: Record for agent and video prompts
headline_features.detail: Turns a narrated screen recording (transcript, click screenshots, links) into a step-by-step action plan or prompt for agents (Rovo, Claude, coding assistants), or into a Jira item. Magic Pen and a Selection tool mark UI elements. Business + AI and Enterprise plans only.
Agents (Claude, Cursor, VS Code, Codex) can pull transcripts, metadata and action items, add timestamped comments, and share or organise recordings. They cannot edit the video.

headline_features.feature: Edit by transcript, plus filler-word and silence removal
headline_features.detail: Trim by selecting words in the transcript. Toggles for Remove filler words and Remove Silence. Business + AI plan.
Loom AI generates titles, summaries and chapters, and runs workflows.

tools.name: Cap (cap.so)
tools.positioning: An open-source Loom and Screen Studio alternative for Mac and Windows: Studio Mode for polished local edits and Instant Mode for share links. Core code is AGPLv3 (the cap-camera* and scap-* crates are MIT). About 24.2k GitHub stars. Ships several times a week. Moved to a native GPUI app in 0.6.1.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Praise: free for personal use, a $58 lifetime desktop licence, open source and self-hostable, custom S3 or Google Drive storage, near-identical Mac and Windows apps, and very fast iteration. Complaints: a younger product with a smaller editing set (per Tella's comparison), free share links capped at 5 minutes, self-hosting falls on you, and some confusion about pricing. Licence note for Frame Job (Apache-2.0): Cap's AGPL code cannot be carried over, the same rule as Concat.

headline_features.detail: Experimental from 0.3.62 (2025-08-06). Spring-based zoom with cursor and display motion blur in 0.5.4 (2026-07-06). Keeps a resting cursor in view, ignores cursor movement in cut sections, and works on multi-take timelines (0.6.1 and 0.6.2).

Custom cursor capture on by default (0.3.67). High-resolution SVG cursors. Hide an inactive cursor with a fade (0.3.74). Smooth and Fast cursor presets, and a cursor-only ProRes 4444 export (0.4.82). Cursor styles with click ripples (0.6.0). Smoothed cursors settle where the mouse stopped (0.6.2).
3D tracks give automatic or custom camera shots with perspective, easing and focus blur. Style tracks change the background, camera or cursor for one section only.
Blur or remove the camera background on macOS, in preview and export (0.6.0). Better removal that keeps only the main person (0.6.1).

headline_features.feature: Keyboard press overlay track and caption tracks
headline_features.detail: A keyboard-press overlay track and caption tracks in the timeline (0.4.81). Local Whisper and Parakeet transcription. Caption presets and animations with SRT and VTT export (0.5.3).
A word-level transcript editor (0.4.82, 0.5.3).

headline_features.feature: Cap for agents: CLI, skill and local MCP server
headline_features.detail: Agents (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor) can record, export, upload and share, and read transcripts, AI summaries, chapters, comments and analytics, with JSON output and confirmation before changes. The notes do NOT say agents can edit the timeline (zooms or cuts).
Built-in teleprompter, clip transitions, and blur and pixelate masks (0.5.7). Scenes with split screen (0.5.1). Decorative frames (0.5.4). Animated gradient backgrounds and Studio Sound (0.6.0).
9:16 area and window presets, and portrait videos fill vertical projects (0.6.2). Image backgrounds are re-cropped when the aspect ratio changes (0.6.1).

Free for personal use (4K60 export, 5-minute links). Desktop $29/yr or $58 lifetime (commercial use, 20 links a month). Pro $12/user/mo ($8.16 billed annually) with unlimited links, AI titles, summaries and chapters, custom domain, password-protected shares, viewer analytics, and custom S3 or Google Drive storage. Self-hosting keeps all features.

tools.name: FocuSee (iMobie)
tools.positioning: A Windows and Mac Screen Studio-style recorder with auto zoom, cursor effects, an AI avatar and a beauty filter. Sold as an annual licence or a lifetime licence.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Picked as the Windows option for Screen Studio-style output, with a lifetime licence ($199.99, or from $49.99/yr per Tella's comparison). Weaknesses: hosting is a paid add-on, there is no team workspace, and advanced AI features need credits.

headline_features.feature: Auto zoom from clicks and typing
headline_features.detail: Auto typing recognition generates zooms from typing (2.4.0 Mac, 2026-07-16; improved in 2.4.1). Smart speed-up of typing sections.
Custom cursor angle, dynamic direction, idle duration, path smoothness, and end position (2.5.0).

headline_features.feature: 3D motion, spotlight, motion blur and keyboard shortcut capture
headline_features.detail: Tilt and perspective that follow the cursor, cursor highlighting, spotlight, motion blur, and keyboard shortcut capture.
PiP and full-screen layouts that switch mid-video, AI background blur or replacement in post, a beauty filter, and custom layout presets (2.5.0).

headline_features.feature: AI subtitles, AI avatar, teleprompter and audio clean-up
headline_features.detail: Subtitles in 50+ languages with SRT import. An AI virtual avatar so you can appear without your face. Teleprompter. Voice enhancement, noise reduction, and filler and silence removal.

headline_features.feature: Resizing for social platforms and share links
headline_features.detail: One-click aspect-ratio resizing for TikTok, YouTube, Instagram and others. Full-screen support for vertical video (2.3.5 Windows). Share links with password and permissions.

tools.name: Prequel (prequel.sh) — new entrant
tools.positioning: A 'cinematic' Mac screen recorder that 'does the editing for you', aimed straight at Screen Studio 4. Launched on Product Hunt 2026-08-30 (198 upvotes, #4 of the day). Ships almost daily. Apple Silicon and macOS 14+ only. All processing is local.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Pitched on price ($39 lifetime or $9/mo, the same app on both) and on matching Screen Studio 4 features within weeks of it. Thin independent feedback so far: one Product Hunt review at 4/5, and a commenter who wanted a lifetime option, which was added at launch. Its own comparison posts are marketing.

headline_features.feature: Auto zoom from clicks and typing, with 3D tilt and yaw
headline_features.detail: Zooms target the cursor, a drawn region, or the field being typed into (typing needs the Accessibility permission). Level, speed, tilt, yaw and blur falloff are set per zoom. Each zoom is an ordinary timeline slice.
A Loupe zoom method (v0.0.35, 2026-10-02) with light spill (v0.1.1). Fisheye zoom (v0.7.0, 2026-10-21).

The pointer is stored as data, not burned into the picture (v0.0.26). Fifteen pointer styles, resized to stay visible during zooms, smoothed while moving, hidden after stillness, and motion-blurred. Click effects (ripples, confetti, chalk), plus click and typing sounds.

Fourteen layouts, switchable per clip. Camera shapes (circle, squircle, rounded, wide, portrait, 'Follow me'). Camera background removal (v0.0.19) and a cut-out layout (v0.8.1). Camera colour looks. Rotation at any angle.

headline_features.feature: Teleprompter in the notch with voice tracking
headline_features.detail: The script sits under the camera notch and highlights each word as it is spoken. It pauses when you go off script and catches up when you skip ahead.

headline_features.feature: Subtitles and edit by deleting sentences
headline_features.detail: On-device transcription. Fix a word by typing over it, or delete a sentence to cut it. Styles: Blur in, Subtitle, Highlight and Band.

headline_features.feature: CLI and a Claude Code skill
headline_features.detail: A `prequel` command-line tool and a Claude Code skill (v0.1.0).

MP4 (H.264 or HEVC) up to 4K and 120 fps, constant frame rate, VideoToolbox plus Metal. Framing is stored as proportions so a layout survives a switch to 9:16. Presets for YouTube, Shorts, TikTok, Reels, X and LinkedIn. Filters (Dream, Dither, Lost signal). Share links involve an upload.
$39 lifetime (5 GB of shared recordings kept 3 months) or $9/mo (unlimited sharing). A 7-day trial with no watermark.

tools.name: ScreenKite — new entrant
tools.positioning: A free native Mac recorder and editor (exports watermarked until Pro) whose pitch is that a local AI agent edits the recording with the same tools the UI uses. Pro is $79.99 one-time for 3 Macs, rising to $99.99 after 2026-10-31. It also publishes aggressive blog posts against Screen Studio.
tools.why_creators_pick_it: Picked by creators who already pay for Claude Code or Codex and want agent editing with no extra AI fee, plus a one-time price. Every source is the vendor's own marketing (version 1.18, September 2026), so treat it as unverified. This is the closest competitor to Frame Job's MCP and Assistant model.

headline_features.detail: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Grok Build and Kimi drive the same editing tools as the UI. Meaning-changing edits return a plan with confirm:false and apply with confirm:true. Edits undo like clicks. There is a CLI (`screenkite agent export --json`). MCP is not stated.
